title.zh: 卷一百七十六 列傳第六十三: 曹伯啟 李元禮 王壽 王倚 劉正 謝讓 韓若愚 趙師魯 劉德溫 尉遲德誠 秦起宗
title.en: Volume 176 Biographies 63: Cao Boqi, Li Yuanli, Wang Shou, Wang Yi, Liu Zheng, Xie Rang, Han Ruoyu, Zhao Shilu, Liu Dewen, Wei Chidecheng, Qin Qizong
title.raw: 卷一百七十六 列傳第六十三: 曹伯啟 李元禮 王壽 王倚 劉正 謝讓 韓若愚 趙師魯 劉德溫 尉遲德誠 秦起宗 Volume 176 Biographies 63: Cao Boqi, Li Yuanli, Wang Shou, Wang Yi, Liu Zheng, Xie Rang, Han Ruoyu, Zhao Shilu, Liu Dewen, Wei Chidecheng, Qin Qizong

sentences.zh: 曹伯啟

translations.literal: Cao Boqi
translations.idiomatic: Cao Boqi

sentences.zh: 曹伯啟，字士開，濟寧碭山人。

translations.literal: Cao Boqi, style name Shikai, was a native of Dangshan in Jining.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Boqi, whose style name was Shikai, came from Dangshan in Jining.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，從東平李謙遊，篤於問學。

translations.literal: At age twenty he followed Li Qian of Dongping in study and was earnest in inquiry and learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he studied under Li Qian of Dongping and pursued learning with great dedication.

sentences.zh: 至元中，歷仕為蘭溪主簿，尉獲盜三十，械徇諸市，伯啟以無左驗，未之信；

translations.literal: During the Zhiyuan era he served in succession as registrar of Lanxi; the district magistrate seized thirty thieves and had them shackled and paraded through the markets; Boqi, because there was no corroborating evidence, did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiyuan period he rose to become registrar of Lanxi. When the district magistrate seized thirty supposed thieves and had them shackled and paraded through the markets, Boqi, finding no corroborating evidence, refused to believe the case.

sentences.zh: 俄得真盜，尉以是黜。

translations.literal: Before long the real thieves were obtained, and the magistrate was dismissed for this.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the real thieves were caught, and the magistrate was removed from office as a result.

sentences.zh: 累遷常州路推官，豪民黃甲，恃財殺人，賂佃客誣伏，伯啟讞得其情，遂坐甲殺人罪。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to investigating censor of Changzhou Circuit; the powerful commoner Huang Jia, relying on wealth, killed a man and bribed a tenant to confess falsely; Boqi tried the case and obtained the true facts, and Jia was convicted of murder.
translations.idiomatic: He was eventually promoted to investigating censor of Changzhou Circuit. A wealthy local bully named Huang Jia had killed a man and bribed a tenant farmer to take a false confession. Boqi tried the case, uncovered the truth, and secured a murder conviction against Jia.

sentences.zh: 遷河南省都事、台州路治中，御史潘昂霄、廉訪使王俁交薦，擢拜西台御史，改都事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to chief clerk of Henan Province and assistant prefect of Taizhou Circuit; Censor Pan Angxiao and surveillance commissioner Wang Yi jointly recommended him, and he was promoted and appointed Western Censorate censor, then changed to chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as chief clerk of Henan Province and assistant prefect of Taizhou Circuit, he was jointly recommended by Censor Pan Angxiao and Surveillance Commissioner Wang Yi and appointed censor of the Western Censorate, later reassigned as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 關陝自許衡倡道學，教多士，伯啟請建祠立學，以表其績，朝議是之。

translations.literal: In Guan-Shaan, since Xu Heng had initiated the study of the Way and taught many scholars, Boqi requested to build a shrine and establish a school to display his achievements; the court deliberation approved it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guan-Shaan region Xu Heng had pioneered Neo-Confucian teaching and instructed many scholars. Boqi petitioned to build a shrine and establish a school in his honor; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 涇陽民誣其尹不法，伯啟核實，抵民罪。

translations.literal: The people of Jingyang falsely accused their magistrate of unlawful conduct; Boqi verified the facts and imposed guilt on the people.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Jingyang falsely accused their magistrate of misconduct, Boqi investigated and held the accusers accountable.

sentences.zh: 四川廉訪僉事闊闊木以苛刻聞，伯啟糾黜之。

translations.literal: The Sichuan surveillance vice commissioner Kuokuomu was known for harshness; Boqi impeached and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: Boqi impeached and removed Kuokuomu, the Sichuan surveillance vice commissioner, who was notorious for his harshness.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，升內台都事，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was promoted to chief clerk of the Inner Censorate and transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In 1314 he was promoted to chief clerk of the Inner Censorate and appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 丞相鐵木迭兒專政，一日，召刑曹官屬問曰：「西僧訟某之罪，何為久弗治？

translations.literal: The chief councillor Temuder held sole power; one day he summoned the officials of the punishment bureau and asked, "The Western monk sued someone for a crime—why has it long gone untried?
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Temuder dominated the government. One day he summoned the officials of the punishment bureau and demanded, "A Western monk has brought suit against someone—why has this case gone untried for so long?

sentences.zh: 」眾莫敢對，伯啟從容言曰：「犯在赦前。

translations.literal: " No one dared reply; Boqi said calmly, "The offense occurred before the amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: " No one dared answer. Boqi replied calmly, "The offense occurred before the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」丞相雖甚怒，莫之奪也。

translations.literal: " Although the chief councillor was very angry, he could not overturn it.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief councillor was furious but could not gainsay him.

sentences.zh: 宛平尹盜官錢，鐵木迭兒欲並誅守者，伯啟執不可，杖遣之。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Wanping stole official funds; Temuder wished to execute the guards as well; Boqi held that this could not be done and had them beaten and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When the magistrate of Wanping embezzled official funds, Temuder wanted to execute the guards as well. Boqi refused and had the guards beaten and dismissed instead.

sentences.zh: 八番帥擅殺，起邊釁，朝廷已用帥代之矣，命伯啟往詰其事。

translations.literal: The commander of the Eight Banners killed without authority, provoking a border incident; the court had already replaced the commander with a new one and ordered Boqi to go and investigate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: A commander of the Eight Banners had executed someone without authority, provoking a border crisis. The court had already replaced him with a new commander and sent Boqi to investigate.

sentences.zh: 次沅州，道梗，伯啟恐兵往則彼驚，將致亂，乃遣令史楊鵬單騎往喻新帥，備得其情，止奏坐前帥擅興罪，邊民以安。

translations.literal: When he reached Yuanzhou the roads were blocked; Boqi feared that if troops went the other side would be alarmed and disorder would ensue; he therefore sent clerk Yang Peng alone on horseback to explain matters to the new commander, fully obtained the facts, and reported only that the former commander was guilty of unauthorized action; the border people were thereby pacified.
translations.idiomatic: At Yuanzhou the roads were impassable. Boqi feared that sending troops would alarm the locals and spark rebellion, so he dispatched clerk Yang Peng alone to explain the situation to the new commander. Once he had the full facts, he reported only the former commander's unauthorized action, and the border region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 大同宣慰使法忽魯丁，撲運嶺北糧，歲數万石，肆為欺罔，累贓巨萬，朝廷遣使督徵，前後受賂，皆反為之遊言，最後伯啟往，其人已死，喻其子弟曰：「負官錢，雖死必徵。

translations.literal: The Datong pacification commissioner Fahuruding transported grain to the northern frontier, tens of thousands of piculs each year, and engaged in fraud on a grand scale, amassing illicit gains in the tens of thousands; the court sent envoys to supervise collection; those who came before and after all accepted bribes and in turn spoke on his behalf; finally Boqi went—the man was already dead—and he instructed his sons and younger brothers, saying, "If you owe official money, even though he is dead it must be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Fahuruding, the Datong pacification commissioner, had transported tens of thousands of piculs of grain annually to the northern frontier while engaging in massive fraud and amassing illicit wealth in the tens of thousands. Envoys sent to collect the debt had all accepted bribes and lobbied on his behalf. When Boqi finally went, Fahuruding was already dead. Boqi told his sons and brothers, "Debts owed to the state must be collected even after death.

sentences.zh: 與其納賂於人，曷若償之於官。

translations.literal: Rather than paying bribes to others, how much better to repay the government.
translations.idiomatic: Better to repay the government than to pay bribes to others.

sentences.zh: 第條汝父所賂之數，官為征之。

translations.literal: Simply list the amounts your father paid in bribes, and the government will collect them.
translations.idiomatic: Simply itemize the bribes your father paid, and the government will collect them on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 」諸受賂者皆懼，而潛歸賂於其子，為鈔五百餘萬緡，民之逋負而無可理者，即列上與免之。

translations.literal: " All who had accepted bribes were afraid and secretly returned the bribes to his son, amounting to more than five million strings in paper money; for the people's overdue debts that could not be settled, he listed them and submitted them for exemption.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who had taken bribes were terrified and quietly returned more than five million strings in paper money to his son. Debts the common people could never repay were listed and submitted for exemption.

sentences.zh: 出為真定路總管，治尚寬簡，民甚安之。

translations.literal: He went out as circuit intendant of Zhending and governed with leniency and simplicity; the people were greatly at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As circuit intendant of Zhending he governed with leniency and simplicity, and the people lived in great contentment.

sentences.zh: 延祐五年，遷司農丞，奉旨至江浙議鹽法，罷檢校官，置六倉於浙東、西，設運鹽官，輸運有期，出納有次，船戶、倉吏盜賣漏失者有罰。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yanyou he was transferred to vice minister of agriculture; by imperial order he went to Jiang-Zhe to deliberate on the salt law, abolished inspection officials, established six granaries in eastern and western Zhe, appointed salt transport officials, fixed periods for delivery, ordered receipts and disbursements, and penalized boatmen and granary clerks who stole, sold, or lost salt.
translations.idiomatic: In 1318 he was appointed vice minister of agriculture and sent by imperial order to Jiang-Zhe to reform the salt monopoly. He abolished inspection officials, established six warehouses in eastern and western Zhe, appointed transport officials, set fixed delivery schedules, regulated receipts and disbursements, and imposed penalties on boatmen and granary clerks who stole or lost salt.

sentences.zh: 歸報，著為令。

translations.literal: On his return he reported, and it was enacted as statute.
translations.idiomatic: He reported on his return, and his proposals were enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 尋拜南台治書侍御史，因言：「揚清激濁，屬在台憲，諸被枉赴訴者，實則直之，妄則加論可也。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Southern Censorate investigating censor and accordingly said, "To exalt the pure and repel the foul belongs to the censorate; for all who come to sue because they were wronged, if it is true then vindicate them, if false then add punishment—that is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed investigating censor of the Southern Censorate. He argued, "Upholding integrity and purging corruption is the censorate's duty. When the wronged come to appeal, vindicate the genuine cases and punish the frivolous ones.

sentences.zh: 今論冤一切不問，豈風紀定制乎？

translations.literal: Now to discuss wrongs and not inquire into any of them—how can this be the fixed regulation of discipline and law?
translations.idiomatic: To dismiss every appeal of injustice without inquiry—how does that accord with the censorate's proper role?

sentences.zh: 」俄去位。

translations.literal: " Before long he left office.
translations.idiomatic: " He soon left office.

sentences.zh: 英宗立，召拜山北廉訪使，時敕建西山佛宇甚亟，御史觀音保等以歲饑請緩之，近臣激怒上聽，遂誅言者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended, Boqi was summoned and appointed Shanbei surveillance commissioner; at the time an edict urgently ordered the building of a Buddhist temple on the Western Hills; censors Guanyinbao and others requested delay because of famine; close attendants enraged the emperor's ear, and those who spoke were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Boqi was summoned as Shanbei surveillance commissioner. An edict had urgently ordered construction of a Buddhist temple on the Western Hills. Censors Guanyinbao and others pleaded for delay because of famine, but court favorites inflamed the emperor, and the remonstrators were executed.

sentences.zh: 伯啟曰：「主上聰明睿斷，是不可以不諍。

translations.literal: Boqi said, "Our lord is intelligent and discerning—one cannot fail to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Boqi said, "Our sovereign is intelligent and discerning—we cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 」乃劾台臣緘默，使昭代有殺諫臣之名，帝為之悚聽。

translations.literal: " He then impeached the censorate officials for silence, saying it would give this illustrious age the name of killing remonstrating ministers; the emperor was startled into listening.
translations.idiomatic: " He impeached the censorate for their silence, warning that the dynasty would be remembered for executing remonstrators. The emperor was shaken into attention.

sentences.zh: 俄拜集賢學士、御史臺侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and attendant censor of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies and attendant censor of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有詔同刊定《大元通制》，伯啟言：「五刑者，刑異五等，今黥杖徒役於千里之外，百無一生還者，是一人身備五刑，非五刑各底於人也。

translations.literal: There was an edict to compile and fix the Comprehensive Institutions of the Great Yuan together; Boqi said, "The five punishments are punishments of five different grades; now tattooing, beating, and penal servitude a thousand li away—with not one in a hundred returning alive—mean one person bears all five punishments, not that each of the five punishments reaches its proper limit on a person.
translations.idiomatic: When ordered to help compile the Comprehensive Institutions of the Great Yuan, Boqi argued, "The five punishments are meant to be five distinct grades. Today a single offender may be tattooed, beaten, and sent to penal servitude a thousand li away, with scarcely one in a hundred returning alive. One person thus suffers all five punishments, rather than each punishment being applied to its proper degree.

sentences.zh: 法當改易。

translations.literal: The law ought to be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The law must be revised.

sentences.zh: 」丞相是之，會伯啟除浙西廉訪使，不果行。

translations.literal: " The chief councillor agreed; but when Boqi was appointed Western Zhe surveillance commissioner, it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: " The chief councillor agreed, but Boqi was soon appointed Western Zhe surveillance commissioner and left before the reform could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，引年北歸，優游鄉社，碭人賢之，表所居為曹公里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding he cited age and returned north, leisurely in village and community; the people of Dang honored him and marked his residence as Cao Gong Lane.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiding reign he cited his age and retired north, living at ease in his home community. The people of Dang honored him and named his lane Cao Gong Lane.

sentences.zh: 伯啟性莊肅，奉身清約，在中台，所獎借名士尤多；

translations.literal: Boqi's nature was grave and solemn; he maintained himself in purity and frugality; in the Inner Censorate he especially encouraged and aided many eminent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Boqi was grave and dignified in character and lived in purity and frugality. While at the Inner Censorate he especially encouraged and promoted eminent scholars.

sentences.zh: 為侍讀學士，考試國子，首取呂思誠、姚紱。

translations.literal: As reader-in-waiting academician he examined the National University students and first selected Lü Sicheng and Yao Fu.
translations.idiomatic: As reader-in-waiting academician he examined National University students and placed Lü Sicheng and Yao Fu at the top.

sentences.zh: 雲南僉事範震言宰臣欺上罔下，不報，範飲恨死，伯啟具其事，書於太史。

translations.literal: Fan Zhen, Yunnan vice commissioner, spoke of chief ministers deceiving the ruler above and misleading the people below; there was no response; Fan died nursing resentment; Boqi set forth the whole affair and recorded it in the Grand Scribe's annals.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhen, a Yunnan vice commissioner, had accused the chief ministers of deceiving the throne and misleading the people. His memorial went unanswered, and he died in bitterness. Boqi set forth the full account and entered it in the historical record.

sentences.zh: 真州知州呂世英以剛直獲罪，伯啟白其枉，進擢風憲。

translations.literal: Lü Shiying, prefect of Zhenzhou, was punished for upright firmness; Boqi declared his wrongful treatment and he was promoted to surveillance duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Shiying, prefect of Zhenzhou, was punished for his upright character, Boqi declared his innocence and secured his promotion to a surveillance post.

sentences.zh: 其好彰善率類此。

translations.literal: His fondness for displaying goodness and leading by example was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His habit of honoring virtue and setting an example was characteristic of him throughout.

sentences.zh: 天歷中，起伯啟為淮東廉訪使、陝西諸道行御史臺中丞，使驛敦遣，伯啟喟然曰：「吾年且八十，尚忘知止之戒乎！

translations.literal: During the Tianli era Boqi was recalled as Huaidong surveillance commissioner and regional censor-in-chief of Shaanxi; courier posts urgently dispatched the order; Boqi sighed and said, "I am nearly eighty—have I still forgotten the warning to know when to stop!
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianli era he was recalled as Huaidong surveillance commissioner and regional censor-in-chief of Shaanxi, with urgent orders sent by courier. Boqi sighed and said, "I am nearly eighty—have I forgotten the warning to know when to stop?

sentences.zh: 」終不起，一時被命者，因相繼去位，天下之士高之。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not take office; those appointed at the same time consequently left office in succession, and scholars throughout the realm honored him.
translations.idiomatic: " He never took office. Others appointed at the same time soon resigned in succession, and scholars throughout the realm held him in the highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 至順三年，長子震亨卒於毗陵，伯啟往拊之；

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhishun his eldest son Zhenheng died at Piling; Boqi went to mourn over him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1332 his eldest son Zhenheng died at Piling, and Boqi went to mourn him.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，卒於毗陵，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year he died at Piling, aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The following second month he died at Piling, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 有詩文十卷，號《漢泉漫稿》，《續集》三卷，行世。

translations.literal: He had ten juan of poetry and prose, titled Casual Drafts from the Han Spring, and three juan of a Continuation, circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He left ten juan of poetry and prose entitled Casual Drafts from the Han Spring and three juan of a sequel, both of which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子六人，孫十人，皆顯仕。

translations.literal: He had six sons and ten grandsons, all of whom rose to prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: His six sons and ten grandsons all attained prominent office.

sentences.zh: ○李元禮

translations.literal: Li Yuanli
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanli

sentences.zh: 李元禮，字庭訓，真定人。

translations.literal: Li Yuanli, style name Tingxun, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanli, whose style name was Tingxun, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 資性莊重，燕居不妄言笑。

translations.literal: His natural endowment was grave and solemn; in leisure at home he did not speak or laugh rashly.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was grave and solemn and never spoke or laughed lightly even in private.

sentences.zh: 歷易州、大都路儒學教授，遷太常太祝，升博士。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Confucian instructor in Yizhou and Dadu Circuit, was transferred to grand invocator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to erudite.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Confucian instructor in Yizhou and Dadu Circuit, then was appointed grand invocator of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and promoted to erudite.

sentences.zh: 定撰世祖聖德神功文武皇帝、昭睿順聖皇后、裕宗文惠明孝皇帝尊諡議，稱頌功德，體制溫雅。

translations.literal: He fixed and drafted the honorific posthumous titles for Emperor Shizu the Sagely Virtuous Divine Meritorious Civil and Martial Emperor, Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, and Emperor Yuzong the Cultured Beneficent Illustrious Filial Emperor; in praising merit and virtue the style was warm and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: He drafted the honorific posthumous titles for Emperor Shizu, Empress Zhaorui Shunsheng, and Emperor Yuzong. His eulogies of their merits were warm and elegant in style.

sentences.zh: 請諡圜丘，升祔太室，禮文多其所詳定。

translations.literal: He petitioned for posthumous titles at the Round Mound and for elevation and enshrinement in the Grand Chamber; much of the ritual text was detailed and fixed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned for posthumous titles at the Round Mound altar and for enshrinement in the Grand Chamber, and much of the ritual text was drafted in detail by him.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，擢拜監察御史，彈劾無所回撓。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was promoted and appointed investigating censor; in impeachment he yielded to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he was appointed investigating censor and impeached without fear or favor.

sentences.zh: 二年，有旨建五台山佛寺，皇太后將臨幸，元禮上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the second year there was an edict to build a Buddhist temple on Mount Wutai; the empress dowager was about to visit in person; Yuanli submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the second year an edict ordered construction of a Buddhist temple on Mount Wutai, and the empress dowager was to visit in person. Yuanli submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 古人有言曰：生民之利害，社稷之大計，惟所見聞而不繫職司者，獨宰相得行之，諫官得言之。

translations.literal: The ancients have a saying: the benefit and harm to the living people and the great plans of the altars of soil and grain—of what one sees and hears without being bound by office, only the chief minister may act on it, and the remonstrating official may speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that matters affecting the welfare of the people and the security of the state—whatever one sees or hears regardless of one's official duties—may be acted on only by the chief minister and spoken of only by the remonstrating official.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷不設諫官，御史職當言路，即諫官也，烏可坐視得失而無一言，以裨益聖治萬分之一哉！

translations.literal: Now the court does not establish remonstrating officials; the censor's duty is properly the path of speech—that is, the remonstrating official—how can one sit and watch gain and loss and not speak a word, to benefit sagely governance by one ten-thousandth!
translations.idiomatic: Today the court has no dedicated remonstrators; the censorate serves as the path of remonstrance and is therefore the remonstrator. How can we sit by watching right and wrong without a word, contributing even one ten-thousandth to sagely governance?

sentences.zh: 伏見五台創建寺宇，土木既興，工匠夫役，不下數万，附近數路州縣，供億煩重，男女廢耕織，百物踴貴，民有不聊生者矣。

translations.literal: I humbly observe that in building the temple on Wutai, once earthworks and timber work began, artisans and laborers were not fewer than tens of thousands; the circuits and prefectures nearby had heavy burdens of supply; men and women abandoned plowing and weaving; all goods soared in price; the people had those who could not make a living.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that construction of the Wutai temple has mobilized tens of thousands of artisans and laborers. The surrounding circuits and prefectures bear crushing supply burdens. Men and women have abandoned farming and weaving, prices have soared, and many can no longer sustain themselves.

sentences.zh: 伏聞太后親臨五台，布施金幣，廣資福利，其不可行者有五：時當盛夏，禾稼方茂，百姓歲計，全仰秋成，扈從經過，千乘萬騎，不無蹂躪，一也。

translations.literal: I humbly hear that the empress dowager will personally visit Wutai, distribute gold and coins, and broadly bestow blessings; there are five reasons this cannot be done: the season is midsummer, the grain crops are flourishing, the people's yearly reckoning wholly depends on the autumn harvest—when the entourage passes, thousands of chariots and ten thousands of horsemen cannot but trample the fields—the first.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the empress dowager will visit Wutai in person to distribute gold and bestow blessings. Five reasons argue against this. First, it is midsummer and the grain is in full growth; the people's livelihood depends entirely on the autumn harvest, yet the entourage of thousands of chariots and tens of thousands of horsemen cannot but trample the fields.

sentences.zh: 太后春秋已高，親勞聖體，往復暑途數千里，山川險惡，不避風日，輕冒霧露，萬一調養失宜，悔將何及，二也。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's years are already advanced; personally toiling the sacred person, going back and forth on a hot journey of several thousand li, mountains and rivers perilous and harsh, not avoiding wind and sun, lightly braving mist and dew—if by chance nourishment is improper, regret will come too late—the second.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the empress dowager is advanced in years. To labor her sacred person on a round trip of several thousand li through summer heat, perilous mountains, wind, sun, mist, and dew—if her health should suffer, what regret could avail?

sentences.zh: 今上登寶位以來，遵守祖宗成法，正當兢業持盈之日，上位舉動，必書簡冊，以貽萬世之則，書而不法，將焉用之，三也。

translations.literal: Since the present emperor ascended the precious throne he has observed the ancestral statutes; this is precisely the time for vigilance and holding fullness; the actions of the exalted must be written in the registers to bequeath standards for ten thousand generations—if written and not followed as law, of what use will they be—the third.
translations.idiomatic: Third, since His Majesty ascended the throne he has observed the ancestral statutes in an era that demands vigilance. The actions of the throne are recorded for ten thousand generations. If they are written but not followed as law, of what use is the record?

sentences.zh: 夫財不天降，皆出於民，今日支持調度，方之曩時百倍，而又勞民傷財，以奉土木，四也。

translations.literal: Wealth does not fall from heaven—all comes from the people; today's support and allocation is a hundred times that of former times, yet again we toil the people and injure wealth to serve earthworks and timber—the fourth.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, wealth does not fall from heaven but comes from the people. Today's fiscal burdens are a hundredfold what they once were, yet we again exhaust the people and waste resources on construction.

sentences.zh: 佛本西方聖人，以慈悲方便為教，不與物競，雖窮天下珍玩奇寶供養不為喜，雖無一物為獻而一心致敬，亦不為怒。

translations.literal: The Buddha was originally a sage of the Western Regions; his teaching is compassion and expedient means; he does not compete with things; though exhausting the world's rare treasures and curiosities in offering, he is not pleased; though not a single thing is offered yet one offers respect with single mind, he is also not angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha was a sage of the Western Regions who taught compassion and expedient means and did not contend with worldly things. He would not rejoice though offered all the world's treasures, nor grow angry though offered nothing at all, so long as the heart was sincere.

sentences.zh: 今太后為國家、為蒼生崇奉祈福，福未獲昭受，而先勞聖體，聖天子曠定省之禮，軫思親之懷，五也。

translations.literal: Now the empress dowager for the state and for the dark-haired people reverently worships and prays for blessing; blessing has not yet been clearly received, yet first the sacred person is toiled; the sage Son of Heaven neglects the rites of fixed attendance and is pained in the thought of kin—the fifth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the empress dowager worships on behalf of the state and the people, yet blessings have not been received while her sacred person is already exhausted. Meanwhile the Son of Heaven neglects his duties of attendance and is consumed with filial anxiety.

sentences.zh: 伏願中路回轅，端居深宮，儉以養德，靜以頤神，上以循先皇后之懿範，次以盡聖天子之孝心，下以慰元元之望。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that midway you turn the carriage shafts, dwell upright in the deep palace, use frugality to nourish virtue, use quiet to nourish the spirit—above to follow the excellent model of the late empress, next to fulfill the filial heart of the sage Son of Heaven, below to comfort the hopes of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that Your Majesty turn back midway, dwell quietly in the deep palace, cultivate virtue through frugality and nourish the spirit through repose—thereby following the late empress's excellent example, fulfilling the Son of Heaven's filial devotion, and comforting the people's hopes.

sentences.zh: 如此，則不祈福而福至矣。

translations.literal: If it is thus, then without praying for blessing, blessing will come.
translations.idiomatic: Thus blessings will come without your having to pray for them.

sentences.zh: 台臣不敢以聞。

translations.literal: The censorate officials dared not report it.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate officials dared not report the memorial.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，侍御史萬僧與御史中丞崔彧不合，詣架閣庫，取前章封之，入奏曰：「崔中丞私黨漢人李御史，為大言謗佛，不宜建寺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade, attendant censor Wanseng was at odds with censor-in-chief Cui Yu; he went to the archives, took the previous memorial and sealed it, entered and memorialized, saying, "Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui privately factions with the Han censor Li and makes great words slandering the Buddha—it is not fitting to build the temple.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 Attendant Censor Wanseng, at odds with Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu, went to the archives, retrieved Yuanli's sealed memorial, and presented it to the throne: "Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui is protecting his Han protégé Censor Li, who has spoken slanderously against Buddhism. The temple should not be built.

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，遣近臣齎其章，敕右丞相完澤、平章政事不忽木等鞫問。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angry and sent a close attendant bearing the memorial, ordering the right chief councillor Wanze, the associate chief councillor Bayan, and others to examine and question.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was furious and sent a close attendant with the memorial, ordering Right Chief Councillor Wanze, Associate Chief Councillor Bayan, and others to investigate.

sentences.zh: 不忽木以國語譯而讀之，完澤曰：「其意正與吾同。

translations.literal: Bayan translated it into the national language and read it; Wanze said, "Its meaning is exactly the same as mine.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan translated and read it aloud. Wanze said, "Its meaning is exactly my own.

sentences.zh: 往吾嘗以此諫，太后曰：'我非喜建此寺，蓋以先皇帝在時，嘗許為之，非汝所知也。

translations.literal: Formerly I once remonstrated on this; the empress dowager said, 'I do not delight in building this temple—it is because when the late emperor was alive he once promised it; it is not something you would know.
translations.idiomatic: I once remonstrated on this myself. The empress dowager said, 'I do not delight in building this temple. The late emperor promised it while he lived—something you would not know.

sentences.zh: '」彧與萬僧面質於完澤，不忽木抗言曰：「他御史懼不肯言，惟一御史敢言，誠可賞也。

translations.literal: '" Yu and Wanseng confronted each other before Wanze; Bayan spoke defiantly, saying, "Other censors were afraid and would not speak—only one censor dared speak; he truly deserves reward.
translations.idiomatic: '" Cui and Wanseng confronted each other before Wanze. Bayan declared boldly, "Other censors were afraid to speak—only this one dared. He truly deserves reward.

sentences.zh: 」完澤等以章上聞。

translations.literal: " Wanze and the others reported the memorial to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " Wanze and the others reported the memorial upward.

sentences.zh: 帝沉思良久曰：「御史之言是也。

translations.literal: The emperor pondered long and said, "The censor's words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pondered at length and said, "The censor is right.

sentences.zh: 」乃罷萬僧，復元禮職。

translations.literal: " He then dismissed Wanseng and restored Yuanli's office.
translations.idiomatic: " He dismissed Wanseng and restored Yuanli to office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改國子司業，以疾卒，贈亞中大夫、翰林直學士、輕車都尉，追封隴西郡侯。

translations.literal: Before long he was changed to vice director of the National University; he died of illness and was posthumously granted Vice Grand Master of the Palace, Hanlin direct academician, and Colonel of Light Chariots, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed vice director of the National University but died of illness. He was posthumously granted Vice Grand Master of the Palace, Hanlin direct academician, and Colonel of Light Chariots, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Longxi.

sentences.zh: 子端，仕至禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His son Duan rose in office to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duan rose to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: ○王壽

translations.literal: Wang Shou
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou

sentences.zh: 王壽，字仁卿，涿郡新城人。

translations.literal: Wang Shou, style name Renqing, was a native of Xincheng in Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shou, whose style name was Renqing, came from Xincheng in Zhuo Commandery.

sentences.zh: 幼穎敏嗜學，長以通國字，為中書掾。

translations.literal: In youth he was keen and clever and fond of learning; when grown he was proficient in the national script and became a secretariat clerk.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and devoted to learning. Proficient in the Mongolian script, he became a secretariat clerk.

sentences.zh: 既而用朝臣薦，入侍裕宗，眷遇特異。

translations.literal: Then through recommendation by court ministers he entered service attending Prince Yuzong and received special favor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by court ministers, he entered service attending Prince Yuzong and received exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，升吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 he was promoted to director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，分置尚書省，遂革。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year the separate Secretariat was established and his post was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287 a separate Secretariat was established and his post was abolished.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，罷尚書省歸中書，復任吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year the Secretariat was abolished and returned to the Central Secretariat; he again served as director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 the separate Secretariat was abolished and he was reappointed director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以婿康里不忽木柄用當道，即自免去。

translations.literal: Because his son-in-law Bayan of the Kangli clan held power in the government, he immediately resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: When his son-in-law Bayan of the Kangli clan came to power, he resigned at once.

sentences.zh: 明年，授大司農丞，不赴。

translations.literal: The following year he was appointed vice minister of agriculture but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed vice minister of agriculture but declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 元貞二年，出為燕南河北道廉訪副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanzhen he went out as deputy surveillance commissioner of the Yannan Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1296 he was appointed deputy surveillance commissioner of the Yannan Hebei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 大德二年，不忽木為中執法，复棄官歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dade, Bayan became chief law officer; he again abandoned office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1298 Bayan became chief law officer, and Shou again resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三年，授集賢直學士，秩滿，就升侍讀學士，俄擢御史臺侍御史，論事剴切。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed direct academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies; when his term ended he was immediately promoted to reader-in-waiting academician; before long he was elevated to attendant censor of the Censorate; in discussing affairs he was incisive and earnest.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 he was appointed direct academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies. At the end of his term he was promoted to reader-in-waiting academician, then soon elevated to attendant censor of the Censorate, where his memorials were incisive and earnest.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，召壽奉香江南，遍祠嶽鎮海瀆。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year Shou was summoned to offer incense in the south and worship at all the mountain peaks, river passes, and sea estuaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1302 he was summoned to offer incense in the south and worship at all sacred mountains, passes, and sea estuaries.

sentences.zh: 密旨：去歲風水為災，百姓艱食，凡所經過，採聽入對。

translations.literal: A secret edict: last year wind and water brought disaster and the people had difficulty in food; wherever he passed he was to gather reports and enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict instructed him that floods and storms had brought disaster the previous year and the people were starving; wherever he passed he was to gather reports for the throne.

sentences.zh: 使還，具奏：「民之利病，係於官吏善惡，在今宜選公廉材幹、存心愛物者專撫字，剛方正大、深識治體者居風憲。

translations.literal: On his return as envoy he fully memorialized: "The benefit and harm to the people depend on whether officials are good or bad; at present one ought to select those who are fair, incorruptible, capable, and cherish things in their hearts to specialize in comforting and nurturing, and those who are upright, firm, and great and deeply understand the body of governance to occupy surveillance duties.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized in full: "The people's welfare depends on the quality of officials. We should appoint fair, capable men devoted to the people's welfare to govern the regions, and upright men of deep political understanding to the surveillance posts.

sentences.zh: 天災代有，賑濟以時，無勞聖慮。

translations.literal: Heavenly disasters come in every age; relief given in season needs no troubling of the sage's concern.
translations.idiomatic: Natural disasters occur in every age; timely relief requires no special concern from Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 惟是豪右之家，仍據權要，當罷其職，處之京師，以保全之，此長久之道也。」

translations.literal: Only the powerful great families still hold crucial power; their offices ought to be removed and they placed in the capital to preserve them—this is the long-lasting way."
translations.idiomatic: Only the great powerful families still hold crucial posts. They should be removed from office and kept in the capital where they can be watched—this is the lasting solution."

sentences.zh: 初，壽與台臣奏：「宰相內統百官，外均四海，位尊任重，不可輕假非人。

translations.literal: Earlier Shou and the censorate officials memorialized: "The chief minister internally governs the hundred officials and externally balances the four seas; the position is exalted and the burden heavy—it cannot lightly be given to unworthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shou and the censorate had memorialized: "The chief minister governs all officials within and balances the realm without. The position is exalted and the burden heavy—it must not lightly be given to unworthy men.

sentences.zh: 三代以降，國之興衰，民之休戚，未有不由相臣之賢否也。

translations.literal: From the Three Dynasties down, the rise and fall of states and the weal and woe of the people have never not been due to whether chief ministers were worthy or not.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Three Dynasties, the rise and fall of states and the welfare of the people have always depended on whether chief ministers were worthy.

sentences.zh: 世祖初置中書省，以忽魯不花、塔察兒、纟泉真、安童、伯顏等為丞相，史天澤、劉秉忠、廉希憲、許衡、姚樞等實左右之，當時稱治，比唐貞觀之盛。

translations.literal: When Shizu first established the Central Secretariat, he appointed Olubuhua, Tachar, Quanzhen, Antong, Bayan, and others as chief councillors; Shi Tianze, Liu Bingzhong, Lian Xixian, Xu Heng, Yao Shu, and others truly assisted at his side; at the time it was called well governed, comparable to the splendor of Tang's Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu first established the Central Secretariat, he appointed Olubuhua, Tachar, Quanzhen, Antong, Bayan, and others as chief councillors, with Shi Tianze, Liu Bingzhong, Lian Xixian, Xu Heng, and Yao Shu assisting them. The age was called well governed, comparable to the splendor of the Tang Zhenguan era.

sentences.zh: 迨至阿合馬、郝禎、耿仁、盧世榮、桑哥、忻都等，壞法黷貨，流毒億兆。

translations.literal: When it came to Ahmad, Hao Zhen, Geng Ren, Lu Shirong, Sangge, Xindu, and others, they destroyed the law and trafficked in goods, spreading poison to the hundred millions.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Ahmad, Hao Zhen, Geng Ren, Lu Shirong, Sangge, Xindu, and others, who violated the law, trafficked in goods, and spread poison to millions.

sentences.zh: 近者，阿忽台、伯顏、八都馬辛、阿里等專政，煽惑中禁，幾搖神器。

translations.literal: Recently Ahutai, Bayan, Badamasin, Ali, and others held sole power, inciting and misleading the inner palace, nearly shaking the sacred vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Ahutai, Bayan, Badamasin, Ali, and others monopolized power, misled the inner palace, and nearly shook the throne.

sentences.zh: 君子小人已試之驗，較然如此。

translations.literal: The tested proof of gentleman and petty man is so clearly compared.
translations.idiomatic: The tested contrast between worthy and unworthy ministers is abundantly clear.

sentences.zh: 臣願推愛君思治之心，邪正互陳，成敗對舉，庶幾上悟天衷，懲其既往，知所進退，天下之事，可從而理也。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes to extend the heart that loves the ruler and thinks of good governance, set forth the crooked and straight in mutual presentation, and set success and failure in mutual comparison, so that perhaps above you will awaken to Heaven's intent, chastise what is past, know what to advance and retreat, and affairs under Heaven may thereby be brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to extend the loyal concern for good governance by setting worthy and unworthy ministers side by side and comparing their successes and failures, so that Your Majesty may awaken to Heaven's intent, learn from past errors, know when to advance and retreat, and bring order to the realm.

sentences.zh: 」九年，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: " In the ninth year he was appointed deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " In 1305 he was appointed deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 十年，改吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was changed to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In 1306 he was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十一年，武宗即位，首拜御史中丞，未幾，更拜左丞，俄復拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Emperor Wuzong ascended; he was first appointed censor-in-chief; before long he was again appointed left vice councillor; soon he was again appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In 1307, when Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Shou was first appointed censor-in-chief, soon made left vice councillor, then again censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 至大二年三月，臥疾求代。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Zhida he lay ill and requested a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of 1309 he fell ill and requested to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，遷太子賓客、集賢大學士。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year he was transferred to mentor of the heir apparent and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1310 he was appointed mentor of the heir apparent and grand academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies.

sentences.zh: 秋九月卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth month of autumn, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 明年，贈銀青榮祿大夫、平章政事、上柱國、薊國公，諡文正。

translations.literal: The following year he was posthumously granted Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master, associate chief councillor, pillar of the state, and Duke of Ji, with posthumous title Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posthumously granted Silver-Green Glory and Blessings Grand Master, associate chief councillor, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Ji, with the posthumous title Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: ○王倚

translations.literal: Wang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi

sentences.zh: 王倚，字輔臣，其先東萊人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, style name Fuchen, his ancestors were people of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, whose style name was Fuchen, came from Donglai.

sentences.zh: 父永福，金末避地徙燕，為宛平著姓，富雄閭里。

translations.literal: His father Yongfu, at the end of Jin fled the land and moved to Yan, becoming a prominent surname of Wanping, wealthy and powerful in the neighborhood.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yongfu fled to Yan at the end of the Jin dynasty and became a leading family of Wanping, wealthy and powerful in the district.

sentences.zh: 倚為人孝友樂易，重然諾；

translations.literal: Yi as a man was filial, friendly, cheerful, and easygoing, and valued promises;
translations.idiomatic: Yi was filial, friendly, cheerful, and trustworthy;

sentences.zh: 與人交，不苟合；

translations.literal: in associating with people he did not join casually;
translations.idiomatic: in friendship he would not join casually with others;

sentences.zh: 讀書務躬行，不專事章句。

translations.literal: in reading books he devoted himself to personal practice and did not specialize in textual commentary alone.
translations.idiomatic: in study he devoted himself to practice rather than textual commentary alone.

sentences.zh: 世祖選良家子入侍東宮，時倚年弱冠，在眾中儀觀獨偉，太保劉秉忠深器重之，即以充選。

translations.literal: Shizu selected sons of good families to attend the Eastern Palace; at the time Yi was just past twenty; among the crowd his bearing alone was imposing; Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong deeply valued him and immediately had him fill the selection.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu selected sons of good families to serve in the Eastern Palace. Yi was just past twenty, and among the group his bearing alone was imposing. Grand Guardian Liu Bingzhong greatly valued him and had him selected.

sentences.zh: 倚服勤守恪，遂見信任。

translations.literal: Yi served diligently and kept to integrity, and thus won trust.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served diligently and with integrity and soon won trust.

sentences.zh: 有詔皇太子裁決天下事。

translations.literal: There was an edict that the crown prince should decide affairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the crown prince to decide state affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡時政所急，民瘼所繫，倚知無不言。

translations.literal: Whatever current policy was urgent or the people's afflictions involved, Yi knew of it and did not fail to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever urgent policy matter or popular grievance arose, Yi spoke of it without reserve.

sentences.zh: 是時，官職未備，而湯沐分邑，地廣事繁，當有統屬，乃拜倚工部尚書，行本位下隨路民匠都總管。

translations.literal: At this time offices were not complete, yet the fief of bath and sustenance was vast in territory and heavy in affairs and ought to have unified authority; he was therefore appointed Minister of Works and acting director-general of civilian artisans under the heir apparent on all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were not yet fully established, but the prince's fief was vast and its affairs numerous and required unified oversight. Yi was appointed Minister of Works and acting director-general of civilian artisans for the heir apparent on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，詔立東宮官屬，以倚為家丞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan an edict established Eastern Palace officials, appointing Yi as household aide.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 an edict established Eastern Palace officials and appointed Yi household aide.

sentences.zh: 又置儲用司，掌貨幣出納，令倚兼之。

translations.literal: The Reserve Supplies Office was also established to manage receipts and disbursements of currency, and Yi was ordered to hold it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: A Reserve Supplies Office was also established to manage currency, and Yi was appointed to head it concurrently.

sentences.zh: 後以疾辭職，仍給太子家丞祿，以優養之。

translations.literal: Later he resigned office because of illness but still received the salary of the crown prince's household aide to support him in comfort.
translations.idiomatic: Later he resigned because of illness but continued to receive the household aide's salary as a generous allowance.

sentences.zh: 倚上言：「不事事而苟竊祿食，臣心誠所未安。

translations.literal: Yi memorialized upward, saying, "Not handling affairs yet idly stealing salary and sustenance—my heart truly cannot be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Yi memorialized, "To draw salary without handling affairs—my conscience cannot be at ease.

sentences.zh: 」不許，力辭再四，方許之。

translations.literal: " It was not permitted; he forcefully declined four times before it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " His request was denied. He pleaded repeatedly and was finally permitted to resign.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，皇孫出鎮懷孟，帝為選老成練達舊臣護之，乃以屬倚。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the imperial grandson went out to garrison Huai-Meng; the emperor selected seasoned and experienced old ministers to guard him and entrusted Yi to him.
translations.idiomatic: In 1289 the imperial grandson was sent to garrison Huai-Meng. The emperor selected seasoned old ministers to accompany him and entrusted Yi to the mission.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝目之良久，謂侍臣曰：「倚，修潔人也，左右皇孫，得人矣。

translations.literal: At audience for farewell the emperor gazed at him a long while and said to attending ministers, "Yi is a man of cultivated purity; to attend the imperial grandson at his side—we have obtained the right man.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor gazed at him a long while and told his attendants, "Yi is a man of cultivated integrity. To have him attend the imperial grandson—we have found the right man.

sentences.zh: 」及行，營幕所在，軍政肅然。

translations.literal: " When he departed, wherever the camp and tents were located, military and civil administration were solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: " On his departure, wherever the camp was pitched, military and civil administration were conducted with strict order.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召還。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，授禮部尚書，以疾辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was appointed Minister of Rites and resigned because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 he was appointed Minister of Rites but resigned because of illness.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: The following year he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈正議大夫、禮部尚書，追封太原郡侯，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Correct Counsel Grand Master and Minister of Rites, enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan, with posthumous title Zhongsu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Correct Counsel Grand Master and Minister of Rites, enfeoffed as Marquis of Taiyuan, with the posthumous title Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: 子二人，鵬，異樣總管府總管。

translations.literal: He had two sons; Peng was intendant of the Yiyang Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons; Peng served as intendant of the Yiyang Directorate.

sentences.zh: ○劉正

translations.literal: Liu Zheng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng

sentences.zh: 劉正，字清卿，清州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng, style name Qingqing, was a native of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng, whose style name was Qingqing, came from Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 年十五，知讀書，習吏事，初辟制國用使司令史，遷尚書戶部令史。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he knew how to read books and studied clerkly affairs; he was first recruited as clerk of the Commissioner for Regulating National Revenue and was transferred to clerk of the Revenue Section of the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he took up reading and clerkly work, was first recruited as clerk of the Commissioner for Regulating National Revenue, and was transferred to clerk of the Revenue Section of the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，罷諸路轉運司，立局考核逋欠，正掌其事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan the transport offices of all circuits were abolished and a bureau was established to assess overdue debts; Zheng directed the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In 1271 the circuit transport offices were abolished and a bureau was established to assess overdue debts, which Zheng directed.

sentences.zh: 大都運司負課銀五百四十七錠，逮系倪運使等四人征之，視本路歲入簿籍，實無所負，辭久不決。

translations.literal: The Dadu transport office owed five hundred forty-seven ingots in tax silver; Transport Commissioner Ni and four others were arrested and bound to collect it; viewing the circuit's yearly revenue registers, there was in fact no debt, yet the case long went unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: The Dadu transport office was charged with owing five hundred forty-seven ingots in tax silver. Transport Commissioner Ni and three others were arrested to collect it, but the circuit revenue registers showed no debt, and the case dragged on unresolved.

sentences.zh: 正察其冤，遍閱吏牘，得至元五年李介甫關領課銀文契七紙，適合其數，驗其字畫，皆司庫辛德柔所書也。

translations.literal: Zheng perceived their wrongful treatment, read through all clerkly documents, and obtained seven documents of receipt for tax silver issued at the barrier in the fifth year of Zhiyuan by Li Jiefu, which exactly matched the amount; verifying the handwriting, all were written by warehouse clerk Xin Derou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng perceived the injustice, searched the records, and found seven receipts for tax silver issued in 1268 by Li Jiefu that exactly matched the amount. The handwriting proved to be that of warehouse clerk Xin Derou.

sentences.zh: 辛貧窘，時已富實，交結權貴，莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: Xin had been poor and straitened but was now wealthy; he had connections with powerful nobles, and no one dared call him to account.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had once been poor but was now wealthy and connected with powerful nobles, and no one dared challenge him.

sentences.zh: 正廉得其實，始白尚書捕鞫之，悉得課銀。

translations.literal: Zheng with integrity obtained the facts, first reported to the ministry to arrest and try him, and fully recovered the tax silver.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng uncovered the facts, reported to the ministry, had Xin arrested and tried, and fully recovered the tax silver.

sentences.zh: 辛既伏辜，而四人得釋，正由是知名。

translations.literal: When Xin had submitted to guilt, the four men were released, and Zheng became famous for this.
translations.idiomatic: After Xin confessed, the four men were released, and Zheng became famous for the case.

sentences.zh: 轉樞密院令史，辟掾中書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs and recruited as secretariat aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to clerk of the Bureau of Military Affairs and recruited as a secretariat aide.

sentences.zh: 十四年，分省上都，會諸王昔里吉叛，至居庸關，守者告前有警急，使姑退，正曰：「職當進而弗往，後至者益怯矣。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the branch secretariat was at Shangdu; when Prince Shiregi rebelled, he reached Juyong Pass; the guards reported an emergency ahead and told them to withdraw for the moment; Zheng said, "Duty requires advancing and not going—those who come later will be all the more timid.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277, when the branch secretariat was at Shangdu, Prince Shiregi rebelled. At Juyong Pass the guards reported danger ahead and urged retreat. Zheng said, "Our duty is to advance. If we hold back, those who follow will only grow more timid.

sentences.zh: 」馳出關，至上都。

translations.literal: " He galloped out of the pass and reached Shangdu.
translations.idiomatic: " He galloped through the pass and reached Shangdu.

sentences.zh: 邊將請黃白金符充戰賞，主者告乏，中書檄工部造給之，後帝以為欺罔，欲詰治。

translations.literal: Border generals requested yellow and white gold tallies for battle rewards; the responsible official reported shortage; the secretariat ordered the Ministry of Works to manufacture and supply them; later the emperor considered this deception and wished to investigate and punish.
translations.idiomatic: Border generals requested gold tallies for battle rewards, but supplies were exhausted. The secretariat ordered the Ministry of Works to manufacture and issue them. Later the emperor considered this deceptive and wished to punish those responsible.

sentences.zh: 正曰：「軍賞貴速，先造符印而後禀命，豈不可乎！

translations.literal: Zheng said, "Military rewards value speed—first manufacturing tallies and seals and then reporting upward, how can this not be acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: Zheng said, "Military rewards require speed. To manufacture the tallies first and report afterward—how can that be wrong?

sentences.zh: 」帝釋之。

translations.literal: " The emperor released the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 十五年，擢左司都事。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to chief clerk of the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was promoted to chief clerk of the Left Section.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬當國，與江淮行省阿里伯、崔斌有隙，誣以盜官糧四十萬，命刑部尚書李子忠與正馳驛往按其事，獄弗具。

translations.literal: At the time Ahmad held the state; he had a rift with Ali Bo and Cui Bin of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat and falsely accused them of stealing four hundred thousand piculs of official grain; he ordered Minister of Punishments Li Zizhong and Zheng to go by courier post to investigate; the case was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad then dominated the government and bore a grudge against Ali Bo and Cui Bin of the Jiang-Huai Branch Secretariat. He falsely accused them of stealing four hundred thousand piculs of official grain and sent Minister of Punishments Li Zizhong and Zheng to investigate by urgent courier. They found no case.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬復遣北京行省參知政事張澍第四人雜治之，竟置二人於死，正乃移疾還家。

translations.literal: Ahmad again sent Associate Administrator Zhang Shu of the Beijing Branch Secretariat and three others to try the case jointly; in the end the two men were put to death; Zheng then pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad sent Associate Administrator Zhang Shu of the Beijing Branch Secretariat and three others to retry the case. The two men were eventually executed. Zheng pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十八年，徵為左司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was summoned as vice director of the Left Section.
translations.idiomatic: In 1281 he was summoned as vice director of the Left Section.

sentences.zh: 十九年春，阿合馬併中書左右司為一，遂為左右司員外郎。

translations.literal: In the spring of the nineteenth year Ahmad merged the Left and Right Sections of the secretariat into one, and he thus became vice director of the combined section.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1282 Ahmad merged the Left and Right Sections into one, and Zheng became vice director of the combined section.

sentences.zh: 三月，阿合馬敗，火魯霍孫為右丞相，復為左司員外郎，謁告歸。

translations.literal: In the third month Ahmad fell; Huoluohusun became right chief councillor; he again became vice director of the Left Section and requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Ahmad fell from power. Huoluohusun became right chief councillor, and Zheng was again appointed vice director of the Left Section before requesting leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 九月，中書傳旨捕正，與參政咱喜魯丁等偕至帝前，問曰：「汝等皆黨於阿合馬，能無罪乎？

translations.literal: In the ninth month the secretariat transmitted an order to arrest Zheng; together with Associate Chief Councillor Zhaixiluding and others he was brought before the emperor, who asked, "You all were partisans of Ahmad—can you be without guilt?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the secretariat ordered Zheng arrested. He was brought before the emperor with Associate Chief Councillor Zhaixiluding and others. The emperor asked, "You were all Ahmad's partisans—can you be guiltless?

sentences.zh: 」正曰：「臣未嘗阿附，惟法是從耳。

translations.literal: " Zheng said, "Your subject never fawned or attached himself—he only followed the law.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng replied, "I never fawned on him. I followed only the law.

sentences.zh: 」會日暮，車駕還內，俱械係於闕東隙地。

translations.literal: " As evening fell the imperial carriage returned within; all were shackled and bound in the open ground east of the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: " At dusk the imperial carriage returned within the palace, and all were shackled in the open ground east of the gate.

sentences.zh: 逾數日，奸黨多伏誅，复械係正於拱衛司，火魯霍孫曰：「上嘗謂劉正衣白衣行炭穴十年，可謂廉潔者。

translations.literal: After several days many of the wicked faction were executed; Zheng was again shackled and bound in the Palace Guard; Huoluohusun said, "Your Majesty once said Liu Zheng wore white clothes and worked in coal pits for ten years—he can be called incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: After several days many of Ahmad's faction were executed. Zheng was again shackled in the Palace Guard. Huoluohusun said, "Your Majesty once said Liu Zheng wore plain clothes and worked in coal pits for ten years—he is incorrupt.

sentences.zh: 」乃免歸。

translations.literal: " He was then released and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then released and sent home.

sentences.zh: 二十年春，樞密院奏為經歷，升參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year the Bureau of Military Affairs memorialized him as administrator and promoted him to deliberator of Bureau of Military Affairs affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 1283 the Bureau of Military Affairs appointed him administrator and promoted him to deliberator of bureau affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，桑哥既立尚書省，擢為戶部侍郎，升戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, after Sangge had established the Secretariat, he was promoted to vice minister of revenue and elevated to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In 1288, after Sangge established the Secretariat, he was promoted to vice minister and then Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉核河間鹽運官虧課事，幾陷於罪，乃移疾歸。

translations.literal: He once reported and investigated the Hejian salt transport official's shortfall in tax quota and nearly fell into guilt himself, and therefore pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He once investigated a Hejian salt transport official's tax shortfall and nearly fell into trouble himself, then pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，桑哥敗，完澤為丞相，复擢為戶部尚書，升參議。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Sangge fell; Wanze became chief councillor; he was again promoted to Minister of Revenue and elevated to deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291 Sangge fell from power and Wanze became chief councillor. Zheng was again appointed Minister of Revenue and promoted to deliberator.

sentences.zh: 尚書省罷，仍參議中書省事。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat was abolished he still deliberated on Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was abolished he continued as deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 湖南馬宣慰庶子，因爭廕不得，誣告其兄匿亡宋官金。

translations.literal: The secondary son of Pacification Commissioner Ma of Hunan, because he failed to win a dispute over hereditary privilege, falsely accused his elder brother of concealing Song official gold.
translations.idiomatic: The secondary son of Hunan Pacification Commissioner Ma, having lost a dispute over hereditary privilege, falsely accused his elder brother of concealing Song official gold.

sentences.zh: 正知其誣，罪之，仍官其兄。

translations.literal: Zheng knew it was false and punished him, while still granting office to the elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng recognized the false charge, punished the accuser, and restored the elder brother to office.

sentences.zh: 濟南張同知子求為兩淮運使，正知其不稱，弗與。

translations.literal: The son of Vice Prefect Zhang of Jinan sought to become transport commissioner of the Two Huai; Zheng knew he was unfit and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: The son of Jinan Vice Prefect Zhang sought appointment as Two Huai transport commissioner. Zheng knew him unfit and refused.

sentences.zh: 張遂作飛語構其事，帝召正詰之曰：「匿金事在右司，爭廕事在左司，參議乃幕長，寢右而舉左，寧無私乎？

translations.literal: Zhang then spread slander to frame the affair; the emperor summoned Zheng and questioned him, saying, "The concealed gold affair was in the Right Section and the privilege dispute in the Left Section—you as deliberator are chief of the staff; you suppressed the right and raised the left—can there be no partiality?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang then spread slander to frame him. The emperor summoned Zheng and demanded, "The gold case was in the Right Section and the privilege dispute in the Left. As deliberator you are chief of staff. You suppressed one and favored the other—were you not partial?

sentences.zh: 」正辨折明，事遂釋。

translations.literal: " Zheng argued and refuted clearly, and the matter was released.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng refuted the charge clearly and was exonerated.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，還清州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he returned to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 1310 he returned to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年六月，以左丞行省江西。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the eighth year he went as left vice councillor to administer the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of 1311 he was sent as left vice councillor to administer the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，改江浙。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he was changed to Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter he was transferred to Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召為中書左丞，升右丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended he was summoned as left vice councillor of the Central Secretariat and promoted to right vice councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Zheng was summoned as left vice councillor and promoted to right vice councillor.

sentences.zh: 二年，立尚書省，懇辭還家。

translations.literal: In the second year the Secretariat was established; he earnestly declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In 1309 the Secretariat was reestablished; he earnestly declined and returned home.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，召諸老臣入議國事，正詣闕言八事：一曰守成憲，二曰重省台，三曰辨邪正，四曰貴名爵，五曰正官符，六曰開言路，七曰慎賞罰，八曰節財用。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong ascended he summoned old ministers to discuss state affairs; Zheng went to the palace and spoke of eight matters: first, preserve established statutes; second, value the provincial and censorate offices; third, distinguish the crooked and straight; fourth, honor titles and ranks; fifth, rectify official tallies; sixth, open the path of speech; seventh, be cautious in rewards and punishments; eighth, economize in wealth and expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, he summoned old ministers to discuss state affairs. Zheng presented eight proposals: preserve established statutes; strengthen the provincial and censorate offices; distinguish worthy from unworthy; honor titles and ranks; rectify official credentials; open the path of remonstrance; be cautious in rewards and punishments; and economize state expenditure.

sentences.zh: 會行赦改元，集議行之。

translations.literal: It happened that an amnesty and change of reign title were carried out; they were gathered and deliberated and enacted.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty and change of reign title were then enacted along with his proposals.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初政，風動天下，正與諸老臣陳讚之力居多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renzong's government the wind moved all under Heaven; Zheng and the old ministers contributed most of the force in presenting and praising reforms.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Renzong's reign reform swept the realm, and Zheng and the other old ministers contributed most to it.

sentences.zh: 累乞致仕不許，拜榮祿大夫、平章政事、議中書省事。

translations.literal: He repeatedly requested retirement but was not permitted; he was appointed Glory and Blessings Grand Master, associate chief councillor, and deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly requested retirement but was refused and was appointed Glory and Blessings Grand Master, associate chief councillor, and deliberator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 時議經理河南、淮、浙、江西民田，增茶鹽課額，正極言不可，弗從。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of managing civilian fields in Henan, Huai, Zhe, and Jiangxi and increasing tea and salt tax quotas; Zheng spoke extremely that it could not be done, but it was not followed.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were discussed to survey civilian fields in Henan, Huai, Zhe, and Jiangxi and increase tea and salt taxes. Zheng strongly opposed them, but his advice was not followed.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，野無麥谷，種不入土。

translations.literal: The year had great drought; in the fields there was no wheat or grain; seed would not enter the soil.
translations.idiomatic: A great drought struck; the fields bore no grain and seed would not take in the soil.

sentences.zh: 台臣言，燮理非其人，奸邪蒙蔽，民多冤滯，感傷和氣所致。

translations.literal: Censorate officials said that harmonizing governance was not in the right persons, the wicked and crooked obscured truth, the people had many wrongs held in abeyance, and this was caused by injury to harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Censors reported that poor governance, wicked officials obscuring truth, and many unresolved popular grievances had disturbed the harmonious order of nature.

sentences.zh: 有旨會議。

translations.literal: There was an edict to convene discussion.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a conference.

sentences.zh: 平章李孟曰：「燮理之責，儒臣獨孟一人，請避賢路。

translations.literal: Associate Chief Councillor Li Meng said, "The responsibility for harmonizing governance falls on the Confucian minister Meng alone—I request to yield the path of worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Chief Councillor Li Meng said, "The responsibility for harmonizing governance falls on me alone as the Confucian minister—I request to yield my post.

sentences.zh: 」平章忽都不丁曰：「台臣不能明察奸邪，臧否時政，可還詰之。

translations.literal: " Associate Chief Councillor Hudubuding said, "The censorate officials cannot clearly perceive the wicked and crooked or judge current policy—they should be sent back and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: " Associate Chief Councillor Hudubuding said, "The censors cannot clearly perceive wicked officials or judge current policy—they should be questioned in turn.

sentences.zh: 」正言：「台省一家，當同心獻替，擇善而行，豈容分異耶！

translations.literal: " Zheng said, "The censorate and secretariat are one family—they ought to offer replacements with one heart, choose what is good and act on it—how can division be allowed!
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng said, "The censorate and secretariat are one family. They should work together in offering counsel, choose what is good, and act on it. How can they be divided?

sentences.zh: 」孟搖首，竟如忽都不丁言。

translations.literal: " Meng shook his head, but in the end it followed Hudubuding's words.
translations.idiomatic: " Meng shook his head, but in the end Hudubuding's proposal prevailed.

sentences.zh: 右丞相帖木迭兒傳旨：廉訪司權太重，故按事失實，自今不許專決六品以下官。

translations.literal: Right Chief Councillor Temuder transmitted an order: the surveillance offices' power is too heavy, therefore investigations lose truth; from now on they are not permitted to decide alone on officials of the sixth rank and below.
translations.idiomatic: Right Chief Councillor Temuder transmitted an order that surveillance offices had too much power and investigations were therefore unreliable, and from then on they were forbidden to decide cases involving officials below the sixth rank on their own.

sentences.zh: 平章忽都不丁、李孟將議行之，正言：「但當擇人，法不可易也。

translations.literal: Associate Chief Councillors Hudubuding and Li Meng were about to deliberate and enact it; Zheng said, "One need only choose the right men—the law cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Chief Councillors Hudubuding and Li Meng were about to enact it. Zheng said, "One need only choose the right men—the law should not be changed.

sentences.zh: 」事遂寢。

translations.literal: " The matter was then laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年卒，後贈宣力贊治功臣、光祿大夫、司徒、柱國、趙國公，諡忠宣。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth year of Yanyou; later he was posthumously granted the title Meritous Minister Who Proclaims Strength and Assists Governance, Glory and Blessings Grand Master, Minister of Education, pillar of the state, and Duke of Zhao, with posthumous title Zhongxuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 1319 and was later posthumously granted the title Meritous Minister Who Proclaims Strength and Assists Governance, Glory and Blessings Grand Master, Minister of Education, Pillar of the State, and Duke of Zhao, with the posthumous title Zhongxuan.

sentences.zh: 子秉德，官秘書監丞，歷兵、工二部侍郎，出為安慶路總管。

translations.literal: His son Bingde held office as vice director of the Palace Library, served as vice minister in the Ministries of War and Works, and went out as circuit intendant of Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bingde served as vice director of the Palace Library, as vice minister in the Ministries of War and Works, and as circuit intendant of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 秉仁，以廕為中書架閣管勾，累官工部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: Bingren, through hereditary privilege, became secretariat archives clerk and rose to Minister of Works before retiring.
translations.idiomatic: Bingren entered through hereditary privilege as secretariat archives clerk, rose to Minister of Works, and retired.

sentences.zh: ○謝讓

translations.literal: Xie Rang
translations.idiomatic: Xie Rang

sentences.zh: 謝讓，字仲和，潁昌人。

translations.literal: Xie Rang, style name Zhonghe, was a native of Yingchang.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Rang, whose style name was Zhonghe, came from Yingchang.

sentences.zh: 祖義，有材勇，金貞祐間，為義軍千戶。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi had talent and courage; during the Zhenyou era of Jin he was a thousand-household of the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi was talented and brave and served during the Jin Zhenyou era as a thousand-household of the righteous army.

sentences.zh: 讓幼穎悟好學，及壯，推擇為吏，補宣慰司令史。

translations.literal: Rang in youth was keen and clever and fond of learning; when grown he was selected and chosen as a clerk and appointed clerk of the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Rang was clever and devoted to learning as a youth. When grown he was selected as a clerk and appointed to the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 國兵取宋，立行中書省於江西，讓以選為令史，調河間等路都轉運鹽司經歷。

translations.literal: When the national army took Song, a Branch Secretariat was established in Jiangxi; Rang was selected as clerk and transferred as administrator of the Hejian and other circuits Salt Transport Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yuan army conquered Song, a Branch Secretariat was established in Jiangxi. Rang was selected as clerk and transferred as administrator of the Hejian and other circuits Salt Transport Directorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，灶戶在軍籍者，悉除其名，以丁多寡為額輸鹽，其後多顧舊戶代為煮鹽，而顧錢甚薄。

translations.literal: Earlier, saltern households on military registers had all their names removed and were assessed salt quotas according to the number of males; afterward many hired old households to boil salt on their behalf, yet the hire money was very thin.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, saltern households on military registers had been removed from the rolls and assessed salt quotas by household size. Many then hired former saltern households to boil salt for them, but paid very low wages.

sentences.zh: 讓言：「軍戶既落籍為民，當與舊灶戶均役，既令代役，豈宜复薄其傭，使重困乎？

translations.literal: Rang said, "Military households having left the register and become civilians ought to share labor equally with old saltern households; since they are ordered to substitute labor, how can it be fitting again to make their wages thin and cause them heavy distress?
translations.idiomatic: Rang argued, "Military households removed from the rolls should share labor equally with old saltern households. Since they are required to substitute labor, how can their wages be kept so low as to crush them?

sentences.zh: 自今顧人，必厚與直，乃聽。

translations.literal: From now on those who hire people must give thick payment before it is permitted.
translations.idiomatic: From now on hires must pay fair wages before approval.

sentences.zh: 」先是，逃亡戶率令見戶包納其鹽，由是豪強者以計免，而貧弱愈困。

translations.literal: " Earlier, absconding households were generally made to have present households cover their salt quota; thereby the powerful and great escaped by schemes while the poor and weak grew more distressed.
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, absconding households' salt quotas were generally assigned to present households to cover. The powerful escaped by schemes while the poor grew ever more distressed.

sentences.zh: 讓令驗物力多寡，比次甲乙以均之。

translations.literal: Rang ordered inspection of material resources' abundance or scarcity, ranked them in grades of first and second class, and equalized them.
translations.idiomatic: Rang ordered a survey of households' material resources, ranked them by grade, and distributed the burden equally.

sentences.zh: 擢南台御史，舉湖廣行省平章政事哈剌哈孫答剌罕可為御史大夫，山東廉訪使陳天祥可為御史中丞，右司員外郎高昉可任風憲。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor of the Southern Secretariat; he recommended Hala Hasun Darkhan, Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, as fit for Censor-in-Chief; Chen Tianxiang, Regional Inspector of Shandong, as fit for Vice Censor-in-Chief; and Gao Fang, Associate Section Director of the Right Secretariat, as fit for censorial duty.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor of the Southern Secretariat, he recommended Hala Hasun Darkhan, Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, for Censor-in-Chief; Chen Tianxiang, Regional Inspector of Shandong, for Vice Censor-in-Chief; and Gao Fang, Associate Section Director of the Right Secretariat, for censorial duty.

sentences.zh: 劾江浙省臣聽詔不恭及不法事，帝遣使雜問，既款服，詔令讓與俱來，人皆危之，讓恬然若無事者，台綱以之益振。

translations.literal: He impeached Jiang-Zhe provincial officials for disrespect in receiving the edict and for unlawful matters; the Emperor sent envoys to question them in detail; once they confessed, an edict ordered Rang to come together with them; everyone thought him in peril, but Rang was tranquil as if nothing were the matter, and censorial authority thereby grew more vigorous.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Jiang-Zhe officials for failing to receive an edict respectfully and for unlawful conduct. After the Emperor sent envoys to cross-examine them and they confessed, an edict summoned Rang to appear with them. Though others feared for him, Rang remained calm as if nothing were amiss, and the authority of the censorate was all the stronger for it.

sentences.zh: 大德間，詔立陝西行御史臺，以讓為都事，凡御史封章及文移，其可否一決於讓。

translations.literal: During the Dade era, an edict established the Shaanxi Branch Censorate; Rang was made Chief Clerk; of all censorial memorials and documents, approval or rejection was decided solely by Rang.
