translations.idiomatic: In the Dade era, when the Shaanxi Branch Censorate was established, Rang was appointed Chief Clerk. Every censorial memorial and document was approved or rejected on his judgment alone.

sentences.zh: 入為中書省右司都事，遷戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered service as Chief Clerk of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat and was transferred to Associate Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Chief Clerk of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat and was transferred to Associate Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時東勝、雲、豐等州民飢，乞糴鄰郡，憲司懼其販鬻為利，閉其糴。

translations.literal: At that time the people of Dongsheng, Yun, Feng, and other prefectures were starving; they begged to buy grain from neighboring commanderies; the Censorate feared they would resell for profit and blocked their grain purchases.
translations.idiomatic: When people in Dongsheng, Yun, Feng, and other prefectures faced famine and sought to buy grain from neighboring commanderies, the Censorate, fearing they would profit by reselling it, shut down the trade.

sentences.zh: 事聞於朝，讓設法立禁，閉糴者有罪，三州之民賴以全活者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the court, Rang devised regulations and established prohibitions: those who blocked grain purchases were culpable; many people of the three prefectures owed their survival to this.
translations.idiomatic: Reported to court, Rang established rules penalizing anyone who blocked grain purchases. Many in those three prefectures were saved as a result.

sentences.zh: 四年，授宗正府郎中，擢監察御史，遷中書省右司員外郎，出為湖廣行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was granted Directorship in the Court of the Imperial Clan, promoted to Investigating Censor, transferred to Associate Section Director of the Right Secretariat of the Central Secretariat, and sent out as Section Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed Director in the Court of the Imperial Clan, promoted to Investigating Censor, transferred to Associate Section Director of the Right Secretariat, and sent out as Section Director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時廣西兩江岑雄、黃聖許等，屢相讎殺，為邊患。

translations.literal: At that time on the two rivers of Guangxi, Qin Xiong, Huang Shengxu, and others repeatedly avenged and killed one another, becoming a border menace.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi's two-river region, Qin Xiong, Huang Shengxu, and others were locked in cycles of blood vengeance, threatening the frontier.

sentences.zh: 讓謂：「此曹第可懷柔，不宜力競，寬其法以羈縻之，使不至跳梁可也。

translations.literal: Rang said, "These fellows need only gentle conciliation; forceful competition is unsuitable. Relax the law to keep them tethered so they do not become unruly—that will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Rang argued, "These people can be won by conciliation, not force. Ease the law to bind them without rebellion—that is enough.

sentences.zh: 若乃舍中國有用之民，爭炎荒不毛之地，非長策也。

translations.literal: If one abandons useful people of the Central Plains to contest barren land in the scorching wilds, that is no long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: To sacrifice useful subjects of the Central Plains for barren frontier wastes is no wise policy.

sentences.zh: 」因書榜招諭，以攜其黨。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he wrote proclamations to summon and instruct them, thereby winning over their factions.
translations.idiomatic: " He posted proclamations to win over their followers.

sentences.zh: 湖廣宣慰使張國紀建言科江南夏稅，讓極言其非便。

translations.literal: Huguang Pacification Commissioner Zhang Guoji proposed levying the Jiangnan summer tax; Rang spoke strongly that it was inexpedient.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Guoji, Pacification Commissioner of Huguang, proposed collecting Jiangnan's summer tax, Rang forcefully argued against it.

sentences.zh: 遷河南行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Section Director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Section Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是時，江淮屯戍軍二十餘萬，親王分鎮揚州，皆以兩淮民稅給之，不足，則漕於湖廣、江西。

translations.literal: At that time over two hundred thousand garrison troops were stationed on the Jiang-Huai front; princes separately stationed at Yangzhou; all were supplied from the popular taxes of the Two Huai; when insufficient, grain was transported from Huguang and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: More than two hundred thousand garrison troops held the Jiang-Huai line, with princes stationed at Yangzhou. Two Huai taxes fed them; shortfalls were filled from Huguang and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 是歲會計兩淮，僅少三十萬石，讓請以淮鹽三十萬引鬻之，收其價鈔以給軍食，不勞遠運，公私便之。

translations.literal: That year accounting of the Two Huai showed a shortfall of only three hundred thousand shi; Rang requested selling three hundred thousand yin of Huai salt, collecting the price in paper money to supply military rations without the trouble of distant transport; public and private alike benefited.
translations.idiomatic: When the Two Huai fell thirty thousand shi short that year, Rang proposed selling three hundred thousand yin of Huai salt and using the proceeds for rations—avoiding long transport and easing both state and people.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，轉戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhida he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時京倉主計吏以倉廩多罅漏，惟久雨米壞，請覆糠粃其上，因揉諸米中，以給內外工人及宿衛者。

translations.literal: At that time the chief accounting clerks of the capital granaries, because the granaries had many cracks and leaks and only after long rain did grain spoil, requested covering the top with chaff and bran and mixing these into the grain to supply inside and outside workers and palace guards.
translations.idiomatic: Capital granary clerks, citing cracks in the stores and rain-damaged grain, asked to cover stores with chaff and mix it into rations for laborers and palace guards.

sentences.zh: 讓察其奸，以藁秸易之，姦弊悉除。

translations.literal: Rang detected their fraud, replacing it with straw, and all corrupt practices were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Rang uncovered the fraud, substituted straw, and abolished the abuse.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜西台治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Western Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Supervising Secretary of the Western Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜治書侍御史，未上，改同僉樞密院事，尋拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Supervising Secretary but before taking office was changed to Concurrent Associate Director of the Privy Council; soon after he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Supervising Secretary but before taking office was made Concurrent Associate Director of the Privy Council; soon after he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，以讓先朝舊人，召見賜酒，以示眷注。

translations.literal: When Renzong was in the Eastern Palace, because Rang was an old man of the previous reign, he was summoned, given wine, to show special favor.
translations.idiomatic: While still crown prince, Renzong summoned the veteran official Rang, treated him to wine, and showed his regard.

sentences.zh: 四年，改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，加讓正議大夫，入謝，賜以卮酒，讓痛飲之。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, Rang was given the title Regular Grand Master of Discussion; entering to give thanks, he was granted a cup of wine and drank it deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On Renzong's accession Rang received the title Regular Grand Master of Discussion. At his audience of thanks he was given wine and drank deeply.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「人言老尚書不飲，何飲耶？

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "People say the old Minister does not drink—why did you drink?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "People say the old Minister does not drink—why did you drink?

sentences.zh: 」讓曰：「君賜，不敢違也。

translations.literal: " Rang said, "It was the Sovereign's gift—I dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: " Rang replied, "It was the Sovereign's gift—I dared not refuse.

sentences.zh: 」少頃，醉不能立，命扶出之。

translations.literal: " After a little while, drunk he could not stand and was ordered assisted out.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was too drunk to stand and had to be helped out.

sentences.zh: 翼日，讓謝，帝曰：「老尚書誠不飲也。

translations.literal: The next day Rang apologized; the Emperor said, "The old Minister truly does not drink.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Rang apologized. The Emperor said, "The old Minister truly does not drink.

sentences.zh: 」初，尚書省柄臣構殺留守鄭阿爾思蘭，籍其家，中外冤之；

translations.literal: " Earlier, a powerful minister of the Ministry of Revenue had framed and killed the garrison commander Zheng A'ersilan and confiscated his property; inside and outside the court all considered it unjust;
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier, a powerful minister of the Ministry of Revenue had framed and killed the garrison commander Zheng A'ersilan and confiscated his property—a verdict widely regarded as unjust;

sentences.zh: 尚書省罷，未有直其冤者。

translations.literal: when the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, no one yet righted his injustice.
translations.idiomatic: and when the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, no one had yet righted the injustice.

sentences.zh: 讓明其事，以所籍貲產給還之。

translations.literal: Rang clarified the matter and returned the confiscated property to his family.
translations.idiomatic: Rang clarified the case and restored the confiscated property to the family.

sentences.zh: 有旨：六部事疑不決者，須讓共議，而後上聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered: when the Six Ministries had doubtful matters unresolved, Rang must jointly deliberate before reporting upward.
translations.idiomatic: An edict decreed that whenever the Six Ministries could not resolve a doubtful matter, Rang must be consulted before it was reported to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是戶部更定鈔法，禮部議正禮文，讓皆與焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon when the Ministry of Revenue revised the paper-money law and the Ministry of Rites deliberated on correcting ritual texts, Rang participated in all.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue revised the paper-money law and the Ministry of Rites deliberated on correcting ritual texts, Rang took part in both.

sentences.zh: 刑部有案，讓未署字，而誤用印，吏懼，遂私效讓署。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Punishments had a case; Rang had not signed his name but the seal was mistakenly applied; the clerk feared and privately forged Rang's signature.
translations.idiomatic: In a Ministry of Punishments case, the seal was applied before Rang had signed. Fearing punishment, a clerk privately forged his signature.

sentences.zh: 事覺，度無損於事，且憐吏以罪廢，遂視之曰：「吾署也。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, judging that no harm was done to the case and pitying the clerk lest he be ruined by crime, he looked at it and said, "This is my signature.
translations.idiomatic: When the forgery was discovered, judging that the case was unaffected and pitying the clerk who would otherwise be ruined, he looked at it and said, "This is my signature.

sentences.zh: 」其寬厚多類此。

translations.literal: " His generosity was often of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: " His generosity was often of this kind.

sentences.zh: 讓上言：「古今有天下者，皆有律以輔治。

translations.literal: Rang submitted a memorial: "From ancient times to the present, all who possessed the realm have had laws to assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Rang submitted a memorial: "From ancient times to the present, every ruler of the realm has had laws to assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 堂堂聖朝，詎可無法以準之，使吏任其情、民罹其毒乎！

translations.literal: How can our glorious Sacred Court be without law as a standard, letting officials follow their whims and the people suffer their poison!
translations.idiomatic: How can our glorious Sacred Court be without law as a standard, letting officials follow their whims while the people suffer!

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 乃命中書省纂集典章，以讓精律學，使為校正官，賜青鼠裘一襲、侍宴服六襲。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered the Central Secretariat to compile statutes and regulations; because Rang was expert in jurisprudence, he was made Revising Official and given one set of blue-rat fur robe and six sets of banquet attire.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the Central Secretariat to compile statutes and regulations. Because Rang was expert in jurisprudence, he was appointed Revising Official and given a blue-rat fur robe and six sets of banquet attire.

sentences.zh: 二年，朝廷以吏多滯事，責曹案不如程者。

translations.literal: In the second year the court, because officials delayed many matters, held responsible those whose bureau cases did not meet schedule.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the court, finding that officials were delaying business, held accountable those whose bureau cases fell behind schedule.

sentences.zh: 令下，讓曰：「刑獄非錢穀、銓選之比，寬以歲月，尚慮失實，豈可律以常法乎！

translations.literal: When the order was issued, Rang said, "Criminal cases are not comparable to revenue or personnel matters; even with months of leniency one still fears losing truth—how can they be regulated by ordinary law!
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, Rang said, "Criminal cases are not like revenue or personnel matters. Even with months of deliberation one still fears getting the facts wrong—how can they be judged by ordinary deadlines!

sentences.zh: 」乃入白於宰相，曰：「尚書言是也。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he entered and reported to the Chancellor, saying, "The Minister speaks correctly.
translations.idiomatic: " He then reported to the Chancellor, saying, "The Minister is right.

sentences.zh: 」由是刑曹獨得不責稽違。

translations.literal: " Thereby the penal bureau alone was exempted from accountability for delay.
translations.idiomatic: " As a result the penal bureau alone was exempted from accountability for delay.

sentences.zh: 拜陝西行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜西台侍御史，命甫下，詔罷西台，復立，就拜侍御史。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Attending Censor of the Western Secretariat; the appointment had just been issued when an edict abolished the Western Secretariat; when it was reestablished he was immediately appointed Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Attending Censor of the Western Secretariat. The appointment had barely been issued when an edict abolished the Western Secretariat; when it was reestablished he was immediately appointed Attending Censor again.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，卒於官，年六十有六。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year he died in office at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year he died in office at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈正奉大夫、河南行省參知政事，追封陳留郡公，諡憲穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Senior Grand Master of the Right and Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu Commandery, with posthumous title Xianmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Senior Grand Master of the Right and Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Chenliu Commandery, with the posthumous title Xianmu.

sentences.zh: 子好古，奉政大夫、覆實司提舉。

translations.literal: His son Haogu held the title Grand Master for Governance and was Commissioner of the Verification Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Haogu held the title Grand Master for Governance and served as Commissioner of the Verification Office.

sentences.zh: ○韓若愚

translations.literal: Han Ruoyu
translations.idiomatic: Han Ruoyu

sentences.zh: 韓若愚，字希賢，保定滿城人。

translations.literal: Han Ruoyu, style name Xixian, was a native of Mancheng in Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: Han Ruoyu, whose style name was Xixian, came from Mancheng in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 由武衛府史授通惠河道所都事，開河有功，詔賜錦衣一襲。

translations.literal: From clerk of the Imperial Guard Office he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Tonghui Riverway Office; for merit in opening the river an edict granted him one set of brocade robe.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as a clerk in the Imperial Guard Office, he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Tonghui Riverway Office. For his merit in opening the river, an edict granted him a brocade robe.

sentences.zh: 遷留守司都事，尋升經歷，出知薊州，改中書左司都事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Garrison Command Office, soon promoted to Administrator, sent out as Prefect of Ji Prefecture, and changed to Chief Clerk of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Garrison Command Office, soon promoted to Administrator, sent out as Prefect of Ji Prefecture, and then made Chief Clerk of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時監燒昏鈔者欲取能名，概以所燒鈔為偽鈔，使管庫者誣服。

translations.literal: At that time supervisors of burning worn paper money wished to win reputation for ability; they generally treated the burned notes as counterfeit and made the treasury keepers confess under false charges.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors charged with burning worn paper money sought to burnish their reputations by treating every note they burned as counterfeit and forcing treasury keepers to confess under false charges.

sentences.zh: 獄既具，若愚知其冤，覆之，得免死者十餘人。

translations.literal: Once the case was complete, Ruoyu knew they were wronged; he reviewed it and more than ten people were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Once the case was complete, Ruoyu knew the men were wronged. He reviewed the case and spared more than ten from execution.

sentences.zh: 遷刑部郎中，提舉諸路寶鈔庫，擢吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, commissioned over treasuries of precious paper money in all circuits, and promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Punishments, put in charge of precious-paper-money treasuries in all circuits, and promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，故事，凡潛邸官吏，不次遷轉，若愚以歲月定其資品，遂著為令。

translations.literal: When Renzong ascended the throne, by precedent all officials of the hidden residence were promoted out of turn; Ruoyu fixed their rank by years of service and this was established as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong ascended the throne, officials who had served him before his accession had traditionally been promoted out of turn. Ruoyu fixed their ranks by years of service, and this was established as regulation.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，遷內台都事，改刑部侍郎，尋擢中書左司郎中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Inner Secretariat, changed to Vice Minister of Punishments, and soon promoted to Section Director of the Left Secretariat of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Huangqing he was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Inner Secretariat, made Vice Minister of Punishments, and soon promoted to Section Director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時議禁民田獵，犯者抵死。

translations.literal: At that time it was proposed to forbid hunting on private fields; violators would face death.
translations.idiomatic: At that time a proposal would have forbidden hunting on private fields, with violators facing death.

sentences.zh: 若愚曰：「昔齊宣王之囿，方四十里，殺其麋鹿者，如殺人之罪，孟子非之。

translations.literal: Ruoyu said, "Formerly King Xuan of Qi's park measured forty li square; killing its elk and deer was punished like killing a person—Mencius criticized this.
translations.idiomatic: Ruoyu said, "In antiquity King Xuan of Qi's park measured forty li square, and killing its deer was punished like murder—Mencius condemned this.

sentences.zh: 」眾以為然，遂輕其刑。

translations.literal: " The assembly agreed and the penalty was lightened.
translations.idiomatic: " The assembly agreed, and the penalty was lightened.

sentences.zh: 時參政曹鼎新辭職，帝曰：「若效韓若愚廉勤足矣，何用辭為！

translations.literal: At that time Vice Administrator Cao Dingxin resigned; the Emperor said, "If you would emulate Han Ruoyu's integrity and diligence, that would suffice—why resign!
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Administrator Cao Dingxin resigned, the Emperor said, "If you would emulate Han Ruoyu's integrity and diligence, that would be enough—why resign!

sentences.zh: 」繼命若愚參議中書省事。

translations.literal: " Ruoyu was then ordered to serve as Associate Administrator of Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " Ruoyu was then ordered to serve as Associate Administrator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 鐵木迭兒為右丞相，以憎愛進退百官，恨若愚不附己，羅織以事。

translations.literal: Temüder served as Right Chancellor; by favor and hatred he promoted and dismissed the hundred officials; he resented Ruoyu for not attaching himself and framed charges against him.
translations.idiomatic: Temüder, as Right Chancellor, promoted and dismissed officials according to personal favor and spite. Resenting Ruoyu for refusing to attach himself, he framed charges against him.

sentences.zh: 帝知其枉，不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew he was wronged and did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor knew he was wronged and refused to act on the charges.

sentences.zh: 拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 延祐六年，命理河間等路囚，輕重各得其情，復拜參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was ordered to judge prisoners of Hejian and other circuits; light and heavy sentences each matched the facts; he was again appointed Associate Administrator of Central Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yanyou he was ordered to judge prisoners in Hejian and other circuits, assigning punishments that fit each case. He was again appointed Associate Administrator of Central Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 丞相鐵木迭兒復入相，以舊憾誣若愚罪，欲殺之，帝不從，復奏奪其官，除名歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Chancellor Temüder returned to office; nursing old resentment he falsely charged Ruoyu with crimes and wished to kill him; the Emperor would not assent; he again memorialized to strip his office, remove his name from rolls, and send him home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Temüder returned to office, he nursed old resentment and falsely charged Ruoyu with crimes, seeking his execution. The Emperor refused, but Temüder again memorialized to strip his office, remove his name from the rolls, and send him home.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，詔雪其冤。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi an edict cleared his wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhizhi an edict cleared his wrongful conviction.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，命復其官，尋拜刑部尚書，遷湖廣省參知政事，未行，改詹事丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was ordered to restore his office; soon he was appointed Minister of Punishments, transferred to Vice Administrator of Huguang Province; before departing he was changed to Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Taiding his office was restored. Soon he was appointed Minister of Punishments and transferred to Vice Administrator of Huguang Province, but before he could depart he was made Vice Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 八月，命宣撫江浙，复留為侍御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was ordered to pacify Jiang-Zhe; then again retained as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was ordered to pacify Jiang-Zhe, but was then retained as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時左丞相倒剌沙擅威福，以事誣侍御亦憐珍等，下樞密獄，無敢言其冤，若愚以計奏左丞相倒剌沙為右大夫，其事遂解。

translations.literal: At that time Left Chancellor Targash abused power; he falsely charged Attending Censors Yilian Zhen and others on fabricated grounds and imprisoned them in the Privy Council; no one dared speak of their injustice; Ruoyu by a stratagem memorialized to appoint Left Chancellor Targash as Senior Grand Master of the Right, and the matter was then resolved.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Left Chancellor Targash abused his power, falsely charged Attending Censors Yilian Zhen and others, and imprisoned them in the Privy Council. No one dared speak for them, but Ruoyu by a stratagem memorialized to appoint Targash as Senior Grand Master of the Right, and the matter was resolved.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢浙西廉使，未行，拜河南省左丞。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to Regional Inspector of Western Zhejiang; before departing he was appointed Left Vice Administrator of Henan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Regional Inspector of Western Zhejiang, but before he could depart he was appointed Left Vice Administrator of Henan Province.

sentences.zh: 會文宗平內難，若愚畫策中機，帝嘉之，進資政大夫。

translations.literal: When Wenzong suppressed the internal turmoil, Ruoyu devised strategy that hit the key; the Emperor praised him and promoted him to Grand Master for Governance.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong suppressed the internal turmoil, Ruoyu devised strategy that struck at the heart of the crisis. The Emperor praised him and promoted him to Grand Master for Governance.

sentences.zh: 天曆三年，遷淮西江北道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianli he was transferred to Regional Inspector of the Huai-West Jiang-North Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianli he was transferred to Regional Inspector of the Huai-West Jiang-North Circuit.

sentences.zh: 九月，以疾卒，年六十八。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he died of illness at age sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he died of illness at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈資德大夫、江浙等處行中書省左丞、上護軍，追封南陽郡公，諡貞肅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Virtuous Achievement, Left Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Upper Guardian of the State; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery with posthumous title Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Virtuous Achievement, Left Vice Administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Upper Guardian of the State, and enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Nanyang Commandery with the posthumous title Zhensu.

sentences.zh: ○趙師魯

translations.literal: Zhao Shilu
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shilu

sentences.zh: 趙師魯，字希顏，霸州文安縣人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shilu, style name Xiyan, was a native of Wen'an County in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shilu, whose style name was Xiyan, came from Wen'an County in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 父趾，秘書少監，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Zhi was Vice Director of the Secretariat; posthumously granted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhi had been Vice Director of the Secretariat and was posthumously granted Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 師魯為人風采端莊，在太學，力學如寒士。

translations.literal: Shilu as a person had dignified bearing; in the Imperial Academy he studied diligently like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu carried himself with dignified bearing. In the Imperial Academy he studied as diligently as a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，為興文署丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou he served as Assistant Director of the Office for Promoting Literature.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yanyou era he served as Assistant Director of the Office for Promoting Literature.

sentences.zh: 五年，遷將作院照磨。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to Assessor of the Directorate of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to Assessor of the Directorate of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 七年，辟為御史臺掾，後補中書省掾，於朝廷典章故實、律令文法，無不練習。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was recruited as clerk of the Censorate; later appointed clerk of the Central Secretariat; regarding court statutes, precedents, laws and regulations, there was none he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was recruited as a Censorate clerk and later appointed a Central Secretariat clerk. He mastered every aspect of court statutes, precedents, laws, and regulations.

sentences.zh: 臨事明敏果斷，執政奇之。

translations.literal: In handling affairs he was clear, keen and decisive; the chief ministers marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: In handling affairs he was clear, keen, and decisive, and the chief ministers marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 及典銓選，平允無私，人無不服。

translations.literal: When he handled personnel selection, he was fair and impartial; no one failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When he handled personnel selection, he was fair and impartial, and no one failed to submit.

sentences.zh: 擢工部主事，遷中書省檢校官，咸著能名。

translations.literal: Promoted to Clerk of the Ministry of Works, transferred to Revising Official of the Central Secretariat—all won renown for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Clerk of the Ministry of Works and transferred to Revising Official of the Central Secretariat, he won renown for ability in both posts.

sentences.zh: 泰定中，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: During the Taiding era he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiding era he was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 時大禮未舉，師魯言：「天子親祠郊廟，所以通精誠，迓福釐，生烝民，阜萬物，百王不易之禮也。

translations.literal: At that time the grand rites had not been performed; Shilu said, "The Son of Heaven personally sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple to communicate sincere devotion, welcome blessings, nurture the people, and enrich the myriad things—it is a rite unchanged through the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the grand rites had not been performed. Shilu said, "The Son of Heaven personally sacrifices at the suburban altars and ancestral temple to communicate sincere devotion, welcome blessings, nurture the people, and enrich the myriad things—it is a rite unchanged through the hundred kings.

sentences.zh: 宜鑑成憲，講求故事，對越以格純嘏。

translations.literal: One ought to mirror established statutes, inquire into precedents, and facing Heaven obtain pure blessing.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to mirror established statutes, inquire into precedents, and facing Heaven obtain pure blessing.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor praised and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 元夕，令出禁中，命有司張燈山為樂，師魯上言：「燕安怠惰，肇荒淫之基；

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival an order issued from within the palace; officials were ordered to erect lantern mountains for amusement; Shilu submitted a memorial: "Ease and indolence in repose lay the foundation of dissipation;
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival an order issued from within the palace directing officials to erect lantern mountains for amusement. Shilu submitted a memorial: "Ease and indolence in repose lay the foundation of dissipation;

sentences.zh: 奇巧珍玩，發奢侈之端。

translations.literal: curious crafts and rare treasures open the beginning of extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: curious crafts and rare treasures open the door to extravagance.

sentences.zh: 觀燈事雖微，而縱耳目之欲，則上累日月之明。

translations.literal: The matter of viewing lanterns is though small, yet indulging the desires of eye and ear would burden upward the brightness of sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: The matter of viewing lanterns is small, yet indulging the desires of eye and ear would dim the brightness of sun and moon above.

sentences.zh: 」疏聞，遽命罷之，賜師魯酒一上尊，且命御史大夫傳旨，以嘉忠直。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was received, he immediately ordered it stopped, granted Shilu one superior measure of wine, and ordered the Censor-in-Chief to convey the imperial message praising loyal forthrightness.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial was received, the Emperor immediately ordered the display stopped, granted Shilu a superior measure of wine, and had the Censor-in-Chief convey an imperial message praising his loyal forthrightness.

sentences.zh: 是時，宰相倒剌沙密專命令，不使中外預知，師魯又上言：「古之人君，將有言也，必先慮之於心，諮之於眾，決之於故老大臣，然後斷然行之，渙若汗不可反，未有獨出柄臣之意，不諮眾謀者也。

translations.literal: At that time Chancellor Targash secretly monopolized commands, not letting inside and outside know in advance; Shilu again submitted a memorial: "Ancient sovereigns, when about to speak, first pondered in the heart, consulted the multitude, decided through old and great ministers, then resolutely executed—dispersing like sweat that cannot be reversed; never has there been one who relied solely on a powerful minister's ideas without consulting the multitude's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chancellor Targash secretly monopolized commands without letting court or country know in advance. Shilu again submitted a memorial: "Ancient sovereigns, before issuing a command, first pondered it in their hearts, consulted the multitude, and decided through old and great ministers—then executed it resolutely, like sweat that cannot be recalled. Never has a ruler relied solely on a powerful minister's ideas without consulting the multitude's counsel.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: " No response was given.

sentences.zh: 倒剌沙雖剛狠，亦服其敢言。

translations.literal: Though Targash was harsh and fierce, he also respected Shilu's bold speech.
translations.idiomatic: Though Targash was harsh and fierce, he respected Shilu's bold speech.

sentences.zh: 有朝士年未及致仕，其子請預廕其官，而執政者為之地，師魯駁其非，事遂止。

translations.literal: A court official had not yet reached retirement age; his son requested advance hereditary appointment to office; the chief ministers paved the way; Shilu refuted the impropriety and the matter was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: A court official had not yet reached retirement age when his son requested advance hereditary appointment. When the chief ministers paved the way, Shilu refuted the impropriety and the matter was stopped.

sentences.zh: 遷樞密院都事，改本院經歷。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Privy Council and changed to Administrator of that office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chief Clerk of the Privy Council and then made Administrator of that office.

sentences.zh: 致和初，升奉政大夫、參議樞密院事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhihe, he was promoted to Grand Master for Governance and Privy Council Deliberator.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhihe era, he was promoted to Grand Master for Governance and Privy Council Deliberator.

sentences.zh: 天歷中，遷樞密院判官，改兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: During Tianli, he was transferred to Privy Council Vice Director and changed to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianli era, he was transferred to Privy Council Vice Director and then made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，特旨起為同僉樞密院事，師魯固辭不就。

translations.literal: Upon mourning his father's death, by special edict he was summoned to resume as Associate Privy Council Commissioner; Shilu firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his father's death, he was specially ordered to resume office as Associate Privy Council Commissioner, but Shilu firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 服除，復為樞密判官，持節治四川軍馬，諭上威德，大閱於郊，寬簡有法，士卒懷其恩信。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he again became Privy Council Vice Director; bearing imperial credentials he managed Sichuan military horses, proclaimed the sovereign's authority and virtue, held a grand review in the suburbs, was lenient and simple yet lawful, and the soldiers cherished his grace and trust.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended, he again became Privy Council Vice Director. Bearing imperial credentials, he managed Sichuan's military horses, proclaimed the sovereign's authority and virtue, and held a grand review outside the city. Lenient and straightforward yet firm in law, he won the soldiers' affection and trust.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷中順大夫、刑部侍郎，樞密院復奏為其院判官。

translations.literal: Before long, he was transferred to Grand Master of Harmonious Accord and Vice Minister of Punishments; the Privy Council again memorialized to make him Vice Director of that office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master of Harmonious Accord and Vice Minister of Punishments, and the Privy Council again memorialized to restore him as its Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為河間路轉運鹽使，除害興利，法度修飭，絕巡察之姦，省州縣廚傳贈遺之費，灶戶商人，無不便之，歲課遂大增。

translations.literal: After some time, he went out as Hejian Circuit Salt Transport Commissioner; he eliminated harm and promoted benefit, restored and tightened regulations, cut off the corruption of inspection patrols, reduced the expenses of post-stations and gift-giving at prefectures and counties; salt producers and merchants all found it convenient, and the annual levy greatly increased.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed Salt Transport Commissioner of Hejian Circuit. He eliminated abuses and promoted public benefit, restored discipline in the regulations, stopped the corruption of inspection patrols, and reduced the costs of post-stations and gift-giving borne by prefectures and counties. Salt producers and merchants alike found the system convenient, and the annual levy rose sharply.

sentences.zh: 暇日，又割己俸，率僚吏新孔子廟，命吏往江右制雅樂，聘工師，春秋釋奠，士論稱之。

translations.literal: On his days of leisure, he again cut from his own salary, led subordinate officials to rebuild the Confucius temple, ordered officials to go to Jiangyou to procure ceremonial music, hired master craftsmen, and in spring and autumn performed the sacrificial rites; scholar opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he again drew from his own salary to lead his subordinates in rebuilding the Confucius temple. He sent officials to Jiangyou to procure ceremonial music, hired master craftsmen, and conducted the spring and autumn sacrificial rites. Scholars praised him widely.

sentences.zh: 師魯由從官久典金谷，每鬱鬱不樂，疾篤，棄官歸京師，至元三年九月卒，年五十有三。

translations.literal: Shilu, having long from attendant office managed finances and grain, was each time gloomy and unhappy; when seriously ill, he abandoned office and returned to the capital; in the ninth month of the third year of Zhiyuan he died, age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Shilu had long served as an attendant official in charge of finances and grain, and he was often dispirited. When his illness grew grave he resigned and returned to the capital, dying in the ninth month of the third year of Zhiyuan at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈嘉議大夫、禮部尚書、天水郡侯，諡文清。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master for Outstanding Counsel, Minister of Rites, and Marquis of Tianshui, with posthumous title Wenqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Grand Master for Outstanding Counsel, Minister of Rites, and Marquis of Tianshui, with the posthumous title Wenqing.

sentences.zh: ○劉德溫

translations.literal: Liu Dewen
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dewen

sentences.zh: 劉德溫，字純甫，大興人，起家中書省宣使。

translations.literal: Liu Dewen, style name Chunfu, was a native of Daxing; he began his career as a Secretariat messenger.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dewen, whose style name was Chunfu, came from Daxing and began his career as a Secretariat messenger.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，以年勞，授從仕郎、內宰司照磨，監建興聖宮；

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, for years of service he was granted Attendant Gentleman and Registrar of the Inner Palace Directorate, supervising construction of the Xingsheng Palace;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Dade, in recognition of years of service he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and Registrar of the Inner Palace Directorate, supervising construction of the Xingsheng Palace;

sentences.zh: 又調承務郎、掌儀署令；

translations.literal: he was then transferred to Gentleman for Service and Director of the Ceremonial Office;
translations.idiomatic: he was then transferred to Gentleman for Service and made Director of the Ceremonial Office;

sentences.zh: 未幾，升奉訓大夫、內宰司丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master for Instruction and Vice Director of the Inner Palace Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Grand Master for Instruction and Vice Director of the Inner Palace Directorate.

sentences.zh: 奉中旨，徵河南民逋糧，德溫輒平其價，令出鈔以償，民甚便之。

translations.literal: By imperial order he collected overdue grain from the people of Henan; Dewen immediately fixed the price and ordered payment in paper currency as compensation, and the people found it very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he was sent to collect overdue grain from the people of Henan. Dewen fixed the price at once and ordered payment in paper currency, which greatly eased the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 复升朝列大夫、延福司丞，奉旨代祠岳瀆。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Grand Master of the Court Array and Vice Director of the Yanfu Directorate, and by imperial order performed sacrifices to the mountains and rivers on the sovereign's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Grand Master of the Court Array and Vice Director of the Yanfu Directorate, and by imperial order went to perform sacrifices to the mountains and rivers on the sovereign's behalf.

sentences.zh: 比還，遷中憲大夫、同知大都路都總管府事。

translations.literal: When he returned, he was transferred to Grand Master of Palace Discipline and Vice Administrator of the Metropolitan Circuit Chief Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was transferred to Grand Master of Palace Discipline and Vice Administrator of the Metropolitan Circuit Chief Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，供億浩繁，德溫措置有法，民用不擾。

translations.literal: Under the imperial chariot hub, supplies were vast and numerous; Dewen arranged matters with method, and the people's livelihood was undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital, where supplies were vast and demands heavy, Dewen managed affairs with sound method and kept the people from disturbance.

sentences.zh: 遷甄用少監，升亞中大夫、禮部侍郎，复升嘉議大夫、同知上都留守司事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of Selection and Employment, promoted to Vice Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Minister of Rites, and again promoted to Grand Master for Outstanding Counsel and Vice Commissioner of the Shangdu Garrison Command.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of Selection and Employment, promoted to Vice Grand Master of the Palace and Vice Minister of Rites, and then to Grand Master for Outstanding Counsel and Vice Commissioner of the Shangdu Garrison Command.

sentences.zh: 省檄和糴糧，民以價不時得，遞相觀望，德溫下令曰：「糧入價出，吏有敢為弊者罪之。

translations.literal: The province issued orders for equitable grain purchase; because the people did not receive payment promptly, they watched one another and held back; Dewen issued an order saying, "Grain enters and payment goes out; any clerk who dares commit fraud shall be punished.
translations.idiomatic: When the province ordered equitable grain purchases, the people held back because payment was not made promptly. Dewen issued an order: "Grain is delivered and payment is issued at once; any clerk who commits fraud will be punished.

sentences.zh: 」於是糧不逾期而集。

translations.literal: " Thereupon grain was gathered without exceeding the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the grain was collected before the deadline.

sentences.zh: 轉大司農丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Granary Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Granary Directorate.

sentences.zh: 耕籍之儀，取具一時，德溫欲考訂典禮，集為成書，未畢，俄授通議大夫、永平路總管。

translations.literal: The rites of plowing and sacrifice were assembled all at once; Dewen wished to examine and revise the canonical rites and compile them into a finished book, but before it was complete he was suddenly appointed Regular Grand Master of Discussion and Circuit Intendant of Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of plowing and sacrifice had been assembled in haste. Dewen wished to examine and revise the canonical rites and compile them into a book, but before he finished he was appointed Regular Grand Master of Discussion and Circuit Intendant of Yongping.

sentences.zh: 永平當天歷兵革之餘，野無居民，德溫為政一年，而戶口增，倉廩實，遂興學校以育人材，庶事畢舉。

translations.literal: Yongping, in the aftermath of the Tianli warfare, had no inhabitants in the countryside; after one year of Dewen's governance, households increased, granaries were filled, and he then established schools to nurture talent; all affairs were fully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping, in the aftermath of the warfare of the Tianli era, had been stripped of its rural population. After one year under Dewen's governance households increased and granaries were filled. He then established schools to nurture talent and brought all local affairs to good order.

sentences.zh: 歲大旱，禱而雨，歲以不歉。

translations.literal: The year suffered great drought; he prayed and rain fell, and the year was not one of shortage.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of severe drought he prayed and rain fell, so the harvest was spared.

sentences.zh: 灤、漆二水為害，有司歲發民築堤。

translations.literal: The Luan and Qi rivers caused harm, and each year the authorities conscripted the people to build dikes.
translations.idiomatic: The Luan and Qi rivers caused frequent damage, and each year the authorities conscripted the people to build dikes.

sentences.zh: 德溫曰：「流亡始集，而又役之，是重困民也。

translations.literal: Dewen said, "The displaced have only just returned, and now to conscript them again would doubly afflict the people.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen said, "The displaced have only just returned, and to conscript them again would only deepen their hardship.

sentences.zh: 」遂罷其役，而水亦不復至。

translations.literal: " He therefore stopped the conscription, and the water also did not return.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore halted the conscription, and the floods did not return.

sentences.zh: 有豪民武斷於鄉里，前吏莫敢治，德溫按得其罪，論如法，杖之，書其過於門，後竟以不道伏誅。

translations.literal: There was a powerful commoner who tyrannized the countryside by force; previous officials dared not punish him; Dewen investigated and obtained proof of his crimes, judged him according to law, had him beaten, and wrote his offenses on his gate; later he was finally executed for immoral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: A powerful local bully had tyrannized the countryside, and previous officials dared not touch him. Dewen investigated, proved his guilt, punished him according to law, had him beaten, and posted his offenses on his gate. In the end the man was executed for gross misconduct.

sentences.zh: 永平，古孤竹國也，國初，郡守楊阿台請於朝，諡伯夷曰清惠，叔齊曰仁惠，為廟以祠之，而祠禮猶未具也。

translations.literal: Yongping was the ancient state of Guzhu; at the founding of the dynasty, the prefect Yang Atai requested of the court posthumous titles for Boyi as Qinghui and Shuqi as Renhui, built a temple to sacrifice to them, but the sacrificial rites were still not complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping was the site of the ancient state of Guzhu. At the founding of the dynasty the prefect Yang Atai petitioned the court to grant Boyi the posthumous title Qinghui and Shuqi the title Renhui, and built a temple to honor them, but the full sacrificial rites had not yet been established.

sentences.zh: 德溫請命有司春秋具牢禮致祭，從之，著為式，賜廟額曰聖清，士論韙之。

translations.literal: Dewen requested that the authorities in spring and autumn prepare full sacrificial offerings and perform the rites; the request was approved, established as precedent, and the temple was granted the plaque title Shengqing; scholar opinion approved.
translations.idiomatic: Dewen petitioned that the authorities perform full spring and autumn sacrifices with proper offerings. The court approved, made it precedent, and granted the temple the plaque title Shengqing. Scholars praised the decision.

sentences.zh: 至順四年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of Zhishun at age sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Zhishun at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈正議大夫、禮部尚書、上輕車都尉、彭城郡侯，諡清惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Correct Counsel Grand Master, Minister of Rites, Upper Colonel of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Pengcheng, with posthumous title Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Correct Counsel Grand Master, Minister of Rites, Upper Colonel of Light Chariots, and Marquis of Pengcheng, with the posthumous title Qinghui.

sentences.zh: ○尉遲德誠

translations.literal: Wei Chidecheng
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chidecheng

sentences.zh: 尉遲德誠，字信甫，絳州人。

translations.literal: Wei Chidecheng, style name Xinfu, was a native of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chidecheng, whose style name was Xinfu, came from Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖天澤，仕金為庫官，郡王帶孫拔絳州，天澤在俘中，道見兵死者，輒涕泣收瘞之，帶孫令佩金符，授雲州御衣局人匠總管。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tianze served the Jin as a warehouse official; when Prince Daison captured Jiangzhou, Tianze was among the captives; on the road whenever he saw soldiers who had died, he would weep and gather and bury them; Daison ordered him to wear a gold tally and appointed him Chief Overseer of Artisans of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau in Yunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tianze had served the Jin as a warehouse official. When Prince Daison captured Jiangzhou, Tianze was taken captive. On the road, whenever he saw dead soldiers he wept and buried them. Daison ordered him to wear a gold tally and appointed him Chief Overseer of Artisans of the Imperial Wardrobe Bureau in Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 父鼎，仕至潞州知州。

translations.literal: His father Ding rose in office to Prefect of Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding rose to serve as Prefect of Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 德誠歷官太子率更丞。

translations.literal: Decheng served in office as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Directorate of Water Clocks.
translations.idiomatic: Decheng served as Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Directorate of Water Clocks.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，改詹事院都事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhide he was changed to Chief Clerk of the Household Administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhide he was appointed Chief Clerk of the Household Administration.

sentences.zh: 二年，遷家令司丞。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Household Steward Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to Vice Director of the Household Steward Directorate.

sentences.zh: 仁宗以為謹恪，常賜酒帛，得侍左右。

translations.literal: Renzong considered him careful and respectful, often granted him wine and silk, and allowed him to attend at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong considered him careful and respectful, often rewarded him with wine and silk, and allowed him to attend at his side.

sentences.zh: 數薦士，出則未嘗語人。

translations.literal: He repeatedly recommended scholars, but once he left office he never spoke of it to others.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly recommended worthy men, but once he had left office he never mentioned it to anyone.

sentences.zh: 事前有粟苗，不種而萌偶出，一莖雙穗，眾以為嘉禾。

translations.literal: Before the office building millet sprouts appeared; though not planted they sprouted by chance, one stalk with twin ears, and the multitude considered it an auspicious grain.
translations.idiomatic: Before the office building, millet sprouts appeared though none had been planted—one stalk bearing twin ears. Everyone took it for an auspicious crop.

sentences.zh: 升家令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Household Steward.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Household Steward.

sentences.zh: 四年，選為河東山西道宣慰司同知，擊姦吏，寬稅斂，上計京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was selected as Vice Commissioner of the Hedong Shanxi Pacification Commission; he struck down corrupt officials, eased tax levies, and submitted accounts in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was selected Vice Commissioner of the Hedong Shanxi Pacification Commission. He struck down corrupt officials, eased tax levies, and went to the capital to submit his accounts.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝方食，賜以馂餘，擢工部尚書，未拜，改陝西行台治書侍御史。

translations.literal: On entering audience the Emperor was just eating and granted him leftover food; he was promoted to Minister of Works, but before accepting appointment was changed to Investigating Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience the Emperor was at meal and granted him leftovers from the table. He was promoted to Minister of Works, but before he could take up the post he was appointed Investigating Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，遷京畿都漕運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he was transferred to Metropolitan Grain Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yanyou he was transferred to Metropolitan Grain Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜遼東道肅政廉訪使，上疏言事，其略曰勞諸王以懷其心，防出入以嚴宮禁，立諫官以遠讒佞，崇科舉以求人材，立常平以備荒年，汰僧道以寬民力，舉賢良以勵忠孝，抑奢侈以厚風俗，及拯鈔法、裁冗官等事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit; he submitted a memorial on affairs of state, the gist of which was: treat the princes well to win their hearts, guard entry and exit to tighten palace restrictions, establish remonstrance officials to keep slanderers and flatterers at bay, honor the civil service examinations to seek talent, establish ever-normal granaries to prepare for famine years, reduce Buddhist and Daoist clergy to ease the people's burden, recommend the worthy and good to encourage loyalty and filial piety, restrain extravagance to strengthen custom, and matters such as rescuing the paper currency system and cutting redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Liaodong Circuit and submitted a memorial on affairs of state. In summary he urged that the princes be treated well to win their loyalty, palace access be guarded to tighten security, remonstrance officials be established to keep slanderers and flatterers at bay, the civil service examinations be honored to seek talent, ever-normal granaries be established to prepare for famine years, Buddhist and Daoist clergy be reduced to ease the people's burden, the worthy and good be recommended to encourage loyalty and filial piety, extravagance be restrained to strengthen custom, and measures be taken to rescue the paper currency system and cut redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 未報而卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: Before a response was given he died, age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Before any response was given he died at the age of fifty-three.

sentences.zh: ○秦起宗

translations.literal: Qin Qizong
translations.idiomatic: Qin Qizong

sentences.zh: 秦起宗，字元卿，其先上黨人，後徙廣平洺水縣。

translations.literal: Qin Qizong, style name Yuanqing, his ancestors were people of Shangdang; later they moved to Ming County in Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Qizong, whose style name was Yuanqing, traced his ancestry to Shangdang; his family later moved to Ming County in Guangping.

sentences.zh: 曾大父當金季兵起，窾山麓為洞，奉其親以居，傍窾大洞，匿其里中百人閉之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather, when warfare arose at the end of the Jin, hollowed out a cave at the mountain foot, brought his parents to live there, and beside it hollowed a large cave in which he hid and shut in a hundred people of his village.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare broke out at the end of the Jin, his great-grandfather hollowed out a cave at the foot of a mountain and brought his parents to live there. Beside it he dug a larger cave and hid a hundred people from his village inside.

sentences.zh: 具牛酒，出待兵，兵入索，惟見其親屬，曰：「孝士也。

translations.literal: He prepared oxen and wine, went out to await the soldiers; when the soldiers entered and searched, they saw only his relatives and said, "A filial man.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared oxen and wine and went out to meet the soldiers. When they entered and searched, they saw only his relatives and said, "This is a filial man.

sentences.zh: 」釋之去。

translations.literal: " They released him and departed.
translations.idiomatic: " They released him and left.

sentences.zh: 里人曰：「秦父生我。」

translations.literal: The villagers said, "Qin's father gave us life."
translations.idiomatic: The villagers said, "Qin's father gave us life."

sentences.zh: 文宗初立，命威順王徵八番。

translations.literal: When Wenzong first ascended the throne, he ordered Prince Weishun to levy the Eight Banners.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong first ascended the throne, he ordered Prince Weishun to levy troops from the Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 是時，蜀省囊加台拒命未平，起宗極言武昌重鎮，當備上流​​之師，親王不可遠去，力止之。

translations.literal: At that time in Sichuan Province Nangiadai's rebellion had not yet been pacified; Qizong urgently argued that Wuchang was a strategic stronghold and ought to prepare forces on the upper Yangtze, that a prince ought not go far away, and forcefully stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Nangiadai's rebellion in Sichuan had not yet been pacified. Qizong urgently argued that Wuchang was a strategic stronghold that must guard the upper Yangtze, that a prince should not go far away, and forcefully stopped the expedition.

sentences.zh: 及王入見，帝謂曰：「八番之行，非秦元卿，幾為失計。

translations.literal: When the prince entered audience, the Emperor said to him, "The expedition of the Eight Banners—had it not been for Qin Yuanqing, would nearly have been a mistaken plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince came to audience, the Emperor said to him, "Had it not been for Qin Yuanqing, the expedition of the Eight Banners would nearly have been a grave mistake.

sentences.zh: 」其後八番師還，無敢擾於道路者。

translations.literal: " Afterwards when the Eight Banners army returned, none dared disturb the roads.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterwards, when the Eight Banners army returned, no one dared disturb the roads.

sentences.zh: 朝議以起宗治蜀，幕府忘其名，曰秦元卿，帝引筆改曰起宗，其眷注如此。

translations.literal: At court it was proposed that Qizong govern Sichuan; the staff office forgot his name and wrote Qin Yuanqing; the Emperor took up the brush and changed it to Qizong—such was his favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the court proposed appointing Qizong to govern Sichuan, the staff office forgot his given name and wrote Qin Yuanqing. The Emperor took up his brush and corrected it to Qizong—such was the regard in which he held him.

sentences.zh: 拜中台御史，劾中丞和尚受人婦人、賤買縣官屋，不報。

translations.literal: He was appointed Censor of the Central Censorate and impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Heshang for accepting another man's wife and buying government buildings at low price; no response was given.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Censor of the Central Censorate and impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Heshang for taking another man's wife and buying government buildings at an undervalued price. No response was given.

sentences.zh: 起宗從台官入見，跽辯久之，敕令起，起宗不起，會日暮，出；

translations.literal: Qizong entered audience with the censorate officials, knelt and argued for a long time; an edict ordered him to rise, but Qizong did not rise; when evening came he withdrew;
translations.idiomatic: Qizong entered audience with the censorate officials and knelt to argue at length. An edict ordered him to rise, but he refused. At dusk he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明日，立太子，有赦，起宗又奏：「不罪和尚，無以正國法。

translations.literal: The next day the crown prince was established and an amnesty was issued; Qizong again memorialized: "If Heshang is not punished, there is no way to rectify the laws of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the crown prince was installed and an amnesty was issued. Qizong memorialized again: "If Heshang is not punished, there is no way to uphold the laws of the state.

sentences.zh: 」和尚服辜。

translations.literal: " Heshang submitted to punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Heshang submitted to punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為御史，當如是矣。

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "To serve as censor—one ought to be like this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "This is how a censor ought to act.

sentences.zh: 」元會，賜只孫服，令得與大宴。

translations.literal: " At the New Year's assembly he was granted a jisun robe and allowed to join the grand banquet.
translations.idiomatic: " At the New Year's assembly he was granted a jisun robe and allowed to attend the grand banquet.

sentences.zh: 又劾閩憲卜咱耳竊父妾以逃，其父憤死，瀆亂天常，流之嶺南。

translations.literal: He again impeached the Fujian surveillance commissioner Bozha'er for stealing his father's concubine and fleeing; his father died of rage; he had violated and disordered heavenly norms, and was exiled to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached the Fujian surveillance commissioner Bozha'er for stealing his father's concubine and fleeing, an offense that drove his father to death in rage. Bozha'er was judged to have violated the order of heaven and was exiled to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 自是盡言無諱，皆見聽用。

translations.literal: From then on he spoke fully without reserve, and all was heard and adopted.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he spoke without reserve, and his counsel was heard and adopted.

sentences.zh: 有《御史奏議》一卷。

translations.literal: He had one fascicle of Memorials of a Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He left one fascicle of Memorials of a Censor.

sentences.zh: 遷都漕運使，帝召諭之曰：「漕輸事多廢闕，賴御史治之爾。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Metropolitan Grain Transport Commissioner; the Emperor summoned and instructed him, saying, "Grain transport affairs have largely fallen into neglect; I rely on you, the former censor, to set them right.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Metropolitan Grain Transport Commissioner. The Emperor summoned him and said, "Grain transport has fallen badly into neglect; I rely on you, my former censor, to set it right.

sentences.zh: 」出為撫州路總管，至官，有司供張甚盛，問其費所從出，小吏不敢隱，曰：「借辦於民。

translations.literal: " He went out as Circuit Intendant of Fuzhou; upon reaching office the authorities' reception provisions were very lavish; he asked whence the expenses came; a petty clerk dared not conceal it and said, "Borrowed and raised from the people.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed Circuit Intendant of Fuzhou. On reaching office he found the reception provisions extravagantly lavish and asked where the expense came from. A petty clerk dared not conceal it and said, "It was borrowed from the people.

sentences.zh: 」遂亟使歸之，幾席僅給而已。

translations.literal: " He immediately had it returned, and his bedding and seats were barely sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately had it returned and kept only the barest bedding and furnishings.

sentences.zh: 自是官府僚佐有宴集，成禮即止。

translations.literal: From then on when officials and subordinates of the government held banquets, they stopped once the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever officials and subordinates held banquets, they stopped once proper ceremony had been observed.

sentences.zh: 因諭眾曰：「我素農家，安儉約，務安靜，庶使吾民化之。

translations.literal: He therefore instructed the assembly, saying, "I have always been of farming stock; I am content with thrift, and strive for tranquility, hoping thereby to transform my people.
translations.idiomatic: He told the assembly, "I come from farming stock. I am content with thrift and seek quiet governance, hoping my people will follow my example.

sentences.zh: 」居一歲，以老去官。

translations.literal: " After one year in office he retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: " After one year he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 明年，以兵部尚書致仕，居一歲，卒，諡昭肅。

translations.literal: The following year he retired as Minister of War; after one year he died, with posthumous title Zhaosu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he retired as Minister of War. One year later he died and was granted the posthumous title Zhaosu.

sentences.zh: 子四人：鈞，銓，鐸，鏞。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Jun, Quan, Duo, and Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Jun, Quan, Duo, and Yong.

sentences.zh: 鈞，西台御史；

translations.literal: Jun was a censor of the Western Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: Jun served as a censor of the Western Censorate;

sentences.zh: 鏞，延徽寺經歷；

translations.literal: Yong was Administrator of the Yanhui Temple;
translations.idiomatic: Yong served as Administrator of the Yanhui Temple;

sentences.zh: 銓，都省掾；

translations.literal: Quan was a clerk of the Metropolitan Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Quan served as a clerk of the Metropolitan Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 鐸蚤卒。

translations.literal: Duo died young.
translations.idiomatic: Duo died young.
